English Language.overview: IBPS PO English tests reading comprehension, vocabulary in context, grammar and sentence structure. Expect passages on banking, economy and social themes, followed by questions on main idea, inference and word meaning. Grammar appears as error spotting, sentence improvement and fillers, so revise subject–verb agreement, conditionals, tenses, prepositions and paired conjunctions such as 'scarcely…when'. Para jumbles reward spotting linking words like 'however' and 'therefore'. Build vocabulary through regular reading of editorials rather than memorising long lists, and practise timed passages to improve speed.
questions:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Financial literacy campaigns often focus on teaching people to save, but saving alone is not enough. A household that keeps all its surplus as cash at home loses purchasing power every year to inflation. Knowing where to save, and understanding the trade-off between safety, liquidity and return, matters as much as the habit itself.
Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
Inflation harms only those households that save regularly every month
Saving well needs knowledge of where and how to save, not just the habit
Financial literacy campaigns have been of no real use to households
Liquidity is always more important than the safety of one's savings

The passage says saving 'alone is not enough' and that knowing where to save and weighing safety, liquidity and return matters as much. It never calls campaigns useless or ranks liquidity above safety.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Once considered a novelty, QR-code payments have become ubiquitous in Indian towns; even roadside tea stalls display a code beside the kettle. Yet this convenience brings a new risk: fraudsters paste their own codes over a merchant's, diverting payments that customers believe they are making to the shop.
As used in the passage, the word 'ubiquitous' most nearly means:
Very expensive
Hard to trust
Rarely noticed
Found everywhere
Ubiquitous means present everywhere. The example of even roadside tea stalls displaying a QR code shows how widespread such payments have become, so 'found everywhere' fits the context.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Once considered a novelty, QR-code payments have become ubiquitous in Indian towns; even roadside tea stalls display a code beside the kettle. Yet this convenience brings a new risk: fraudsters paste their own codes over a merchant's, diverting payments that customers believe they are making to the shop.
According to the passage, how do fraudsters divert payments meant for merchants?
By hacking into the bank accounts of the roadside tea stalls
By asking customers to pay in cash instead of by QR code
By covering the merchant's QR code with a code of their own
By printing fake currency notes and passing them to shopkeepers
The passage states that fraudsters paste their own codes over a merchant's, so customers unknowingly pay the fraudster. Hacking accounts or fake notes is not mentioned anywhere in the passage.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The committee's report was so ________ that even experts found it difficult to follow.
lucid
convoluted
concise
candid
Convoluted means extremely complex and hard to follow, which matches 'even experts found it difficult'. Lucid and concise mean clear and brief, which contradict the sentence; candid means frank.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
Every bank must ________ with the know-your-customer norms before opening a new account.
comply
compile
compel
complain
'Comply with' means to act in accordance with a rule, which is what banks must do with KYC norms. Compile, compel and complain are similar-sounding but do not fit with 'with the norms'.

Choose the pair of words that best fills both blanks.
The new policy was ________ by the board, but its implementation was ________ due to a shortage of funds.
rejected, hastened
approved, accelerated
opposed, completed
approved, delayed
'But' signals contrast: the board approved the policy, yet a fund shortage delayed it. A shortage of funds cannot logically accelerate or complete implementation, so the other pairs fail.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The number of customers (A) / visiting the branch (B) / have increased sharply (C) / since last year. (D)
The subject is 'the number', which is singular, so the verb must be 'has increased'. Contrast 'a number of customers have', where the plural verb would be correct. The error is in part (C).

Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
If I was (A) / in your place, (B) / I would accept (C) / the transfer offer. (D)
In an imaginary or hypothetical condition, the subjunctive 'were' is used with all subjects: 'If I were in your place'. Hence part (A) contains the error; the rest is correct.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
He insisted ON TO PAY the bill himself.
on paying
to pay
for paying
No improvement required
The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' followed by a gerund: 'insisted on paying'. 'Insisted to pay' and 'insisted for paying' are incorrect usages, so the sentence needs improvement.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
Scarcely had she reached the station WHEN THE TRAIN LEFT.
than the train left
then the train left
when the train had left
No improvement required
'Scarcely' pairs with 'when' (just as 'no sooner' pairs with 'than'), and the past perfect belongs in the first clause. So the sentence is already correct; 'than' is a common trap.

Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P: With a microloan from a self-help group, she finally bought her first machine.
Q: Meena had always wanted to start a small tailoring business at home.
R: Within a year, she was earning enough to repay the loan and hire a helper.
S: However, she lacked the money to buy even a single sewing machine.
SQPR
QPSR
QSPR
PQSR
Q introduces Meena's wish, S states the obstacle with 'However', P resolves it through the microloan, and R gives the result a year later. Hence QSPR forms the logical sequence.
Select the synonym of the given word: AMELIORATE
Worsen
Improve
Ignore
Complicate
To ameliorate is to make something bad or unsatisfactory better, so 'improve' is the synonym. 'Worsen' is its opposite, and ignore or complicate do not carry the sense of making better.
Pick the antonym of OBSCURE from the options given below.
Evident
Hidden
Vague
Murky
Obscure means not clear or hard to understand. 'Evident' means plainly visible or clear, making it the antonym. Hidden, vague and murky are close in meaning to obscure, not opposite.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To bite the bullet'.
To speak rudely to a senior colleague
To make a hasty decision without thinking
To avoid a problem for as long as possible
To face a painful situation with courage
'Bite the bullet' means to accept and face something unpleasant or difficult bravely, for example accepting a tough cost-cutting decision. Avoiding a problem is the opposite of its meaning.
Choose the word that is INCORRECTLY spelt.
Embarrass
Occurrence
Millenium
Questionnaire
The correct spelling is 'Millennium', with double l and double n. Embarrass (double r, double s), occurrence (double c, double r) and questionnaire (double n) are all spelt correctly.

Quantitative Aptitude.overview: This section covers simplification and approximation, number series, quadratic equations, and arithmetic topics such as percentages, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, partnership, time and work, speed and distance, boats, mixtures and alligation, mensuration, probability and permutations. Data interpretation sets carry heavy weight in the Mains. Focus on quick calculation tricks, fractions-to-percentage conversions, and multiplier methods for successive changes. Always write units and check whether a question asks for an exact or approximate value.
questions:
What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?)
39.97% of 1200.05 + 14.98² = ?
Round off: 40% of 1200 = 480 and 15² = 225. So the value is about 480 + 225 = 705. Rounding to the nearest convenient numbers first saves time in the exam.

What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the series?
5, 11, 24, 51, 106, ?
Each term is double the previous term plus an increasing number: ×2+1, ×2+2, ×2+3, ×2+4. Next: 106 × 2 + 5 = 217.

Find the roots of each quadratic below and decide how x relates to y.
I. x² − 9x + 20 = 0
II. y² − 11y + 30 = 0
x < y
x > y
x ≤ y
Relationship cannot be established
I gives x = 4 or 5; II gives y = 5 or 6. Every x is less than or equal to every y, and x = y = 5 is possible, so the relationship is x ≤ y, not strictly x < y.
Ravi's salary is first raised by 25% and then the new salary is reduced by 20%. What is the net change in his salary?
5% increase
No change
5% decrease
2% increase
Net multiplier = 1.25 × 0.80 = 1.00, so there is no change. Simply subtracting 20 from 25 to get a 5% increase is wrong because the 20% cut applies to the larger raised salary.
A trader sells two mobile phones at ₹9,600 each. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. What is his overall result?
Loss of ₹800
No profit, no loss
Gain of ₹800
Loss of ₹400
Cost prices are 9600/1.2 = ₹8,000 and 9600/0.8 = ₹12,000, total ₹20,000. Selling price is ₹19,200, so the loss is ₹800 (4%). Equal gain and loss percentages on equal SPs always mean a loss.
What is the compound interest on ₹20,000 for 1 year at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
Half-yearly compounding gives 5% per half-year for 2 periods. Amount = 20,000 × 1.05² = ₹22,050, so CI = ₹2,050. Simple interest would be ₹2,000, the tempting wrong option.
P, Q and R invest in a business in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. P keeps the money for 12 months, Q for 9 months and R for 6 months. Out of an annual profit of ₹34,000, what is R's share?
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time: 36 : 36 : 30 = 6 : 6 : 5. R's share = 5/17 × 34,000 = ₹10,000. Ignoring time and using 3 : 4 : 5 would wrongly favour R.
A and B together can finish a job in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, and C and A together in 20 days. In how many days can A alone finish the job?
24 days
30 days
40 days
20 days
Adding the three pairs: 2(A + B + C) = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 1/5, so A + B + C = 1/10 per day. A = 1/10 − (B + C) = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. A alone takes 30 days.
Two trains 180 m and 120 m long are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. In how many seconds will they completely cross each other?
12 seconds
15 seconds
20 seconds
10 seconds
In opposite directions speeds add: 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Total length to cover = 180 + 120 = 300 m. Time = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 seconds. Using the difference of speeds would give 60 seconds.
A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. The boat goes 36 km downstream and returns to the start. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
15 km/h
14 km/h
Downstream 18 km/h takes 2 h; upstream 12 km/h takes 3 h. Total distance 72 km in 5 h gives 14.4 km/h. It is less than 15 km/h because more time is spent at the slower upstream speed.
In what ratio must rice costing ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹55 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹45 per kg?
By alligation: cheaper : dearer = (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1. Since ₹45 is closer to ₹40, more of the cheaper rice is needed, which rules out 1 : 2.
What is the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
440 cm²
308 cm²
880 cm²
Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 10 = 440 cm². 1,540 cm³ would be the volume (πr²h), a common confusion, and 880 cm² doubles the correct value.
Three fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at least two heads?
Of 8 equally likely outcomes, exactly two heads occur in 3 (HHT, HTH, THH) and three heads in 1. So P = 4/8 = 1/2. 3/8 counts only 'exactly two heads' and misses HHH.
In how many ways can a committee of 3 men and 2 women be formed from 6 men and 5 women?
Choose men and women independently and multiply: 6C3 × 5C2 = 20 × 10 = 200. 252 is 10C5, which ignores the condition of exactly 3 men and 2 women.

The table shows total deposits (₹ crore) of a bank branch.
2021 – 420, 2022 – 480, 2023 – 552, 2024 – 600
What is the percentage increase in deposits from 2022 to 2023?
Increase = 552 − 480 = 72. Percentage increase = 72 ÷ 480 × 100 = 15%. Dividing by the later year's value (552) gives about 13% and is a common mistake; always divide by the base year.

Reasoning Ability.overview: Reasoning in IBPS PO includes seating and floor puzzles, syllogisms, inequalities, blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding, ranking, alphanumeric series, ordering and critical reasoning such as assumptions. Puzzles carry the most marks, so practise drawing quick tables and testing cases systematically. For syllogisms use Venn diagrams and remember the 'possibility' type. In inequalities, link statements through common terms. Read each condition carefully and avoid assumptions about gender or direction not given in the question.
questions:
Five persons P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a five-storey building; the ground floor is numbered 1 and the top floor 5.
• Only two persons live between P and T, and P lives above T.
• S lives immediately above T.
• Q lives on an even-numbered floor.
• R lives below S.
Who lives on floor 1?
T
Q
S
R
P above T with two between gives T on 1 or 2. T on 1 forces Q onto an odd floor, so T = 2, S = 3, P = 5. Q must be on 4 (even), leaving R on floor 1.

Five persons P, Q, R, S and T live on different floors of a five-storey building; the ground floor is numbered 1 and the top floor 5.
• Only two persons live between P and T, and P lives above T.
• S lives immediately above T.
• Q lives on an even-numbered floor.
• R lives below S.
How many persons live between Q and R?
One
Three
None
Two
The arrangement is R (1), T (2), S (3), Q (4), P (5). Between Q on floor 4 and R on floor 1 live T and S, that is two persons.

Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row facing north.
• C sits third from the left end.
• Only one person sits between C and F.
• A sits immediately to the right of F.
• B sits at one of the extreme ends.
• D is not an immediate neighbour of C.
Who sits second from the right end?
E
B
D
A
F cannot be at position 5 (A must be on its right), so F is 1st and A 2nd. B takes the right end. D cannot be 4th (next to C), so D is 5th and E 4th: F A C E D B.

Statements: All accounts are deposits. Some deposits are loans. No loan is a bond.
Conclusions: I. Some accounts are loans. II. Some deposits are not bonds.
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows

Accounts lie inside deposits, but the deposits that are loans may lie outside accounts, so I is not certain. The deposits that are loans can never be bonds, so some deposits are definitely not bonds. Only II follows.

Statements: Some cards are coins. No coin is a key.
Conclusions: I. Some cards are not keys. II. All keys being cards is a possibility.
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
The cards that are coins cannot be keys, so I definitely follows. Nothing prevents keys from lying entirely inside the card circle (outside coins), so the possibility in II also holds. Both follow.

In the following question, the relationship between different elements is shown. Decide which conclusion(s) definitely hold true.
Given: P ≥ Q = R > S; T ≥ R
Conclusions: I. T > S  II. P > T
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Combining, T ≥ R > S gives T > S, so I follows. P and T are both only known to be ≥ R, so their relative order cannot be fixed and II does not follow. Only I follows.
Pointing to a woman, Karan said, 'Her mother's only son is my father.' How is the woman related to Karan?
Aunt
Sister
Mother
Cousin
The only son of the woman's mother is the woman's brother, and he is Karan's father. So the woman is the sister of Karan's father, which makes her Karan's aunt (paternal aunt).

P # Q means P is the father of Q; P @ Q means P is the sister of Q; P $ Q means P is the wife of Q.
In the expression M $ N # O @ R, how is R related to M?
Daughter only
Son or daughter
Niece
Sister
M is N's wife and N is O's father, so M is O's mother. O is R's sister, so R is also a child of M. R's gender is not given, so R is M's son or daughter.
Priya walks 8 m south, turns left and walks 6 m, turns left again and walks 14 m, then turns right and walks 2 m. How far and in which direction is she from her starting point?
10 m, North-East
10 m, South-East
14 m, North-East
8 m, North
South 8 then left (east) 6, left (north) 14, right (east) 2. Net: 8 m east and 6 m north of the start. Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m, towards the North-East.
In a certain code language, PLANT is written as QNDRY. How is GRAIN written in that code?
HTDLS
HSDMS
HTCMS
HTDMS
Each letter moves forward by its position: +1, +2, +3, +4, +5 (P→Q, L→N, A→D, N→R, T→Y). Applying the same to GRAIN: G→H, R→T, A→D, I→M, N→S, giving HTDMS.
In a code language, 'bank gives loan' is written as 'mo ta zi', 'loan is cheap' as 'zi ka pu' and 'cheap bank rate' as 'pu mo xe'. What is the code for 'gives'?
mo
zi
ta
ka
'bank' is common to sentences 1 and 3 (mo), 'loan' to 1 and 2 (zi), 'cheap' to 2 and 3 (pu). In sentence 1, the remaining code ta must stand for 'gives'.
In a row of students, Kiran is 15th from the left end. When she moves six places to her right, she becomes 22nd from the right end. How many students are there in the row?
After moving six places right, Kiran is 21st from the left and 22nd from the right. Total = 21 + 22 − 1 = 42. Using her original 15th position with 22 would give the wrong answer.

Study the arrangement:
R 4 % T 7 K @ 2 M 9 # E 5 $ U 3 & B
How many numbers in the arrangement are immediately followed by a symbol?
Four
Three
Two
Five
The number–symbol pairs are 4 %, 9 #, 5 $ and 3 &, so four numbers qualify. 7 is followed by K and 2 by M, so they are excluded.
Among J, K, L, M and N, each of a different weight: K is heavier than both M and N but lighter than L. M is heavier than N. J is lighter than N. Who is the lightest?
N
M
K
J
From the clues, L > K > M > N, and J is lighter than N. So the order is L > K > M > N > J, making J the lightest. N is second-lightest, a tempting trap.

Statement: A bank announces that customers who register their mobile number will receive an SMS alert for every transaction in their account.
Which of the following is implicit in the statement?
Customers who do not own mobile phones will close their accounts soon
SMS alerts will completely eliminate all kinds of banking frauds
Many customers would like to be informed of transactions in their account
The bank has never informed its customers about any transaction earlier
Offering alerts assumes customers value being informed about their transactions. Claims about closing accounts, ending all fraud, or past bank practice go beyond the statement and are not assumed.

English Language.overview: IBPS Clerk English checks basic grammar, vocabulary and reading skills. Expect a short passage with factual and word-meaning questions, fillers, error spotting, sentence improvement, para jumbles and vocabulary items such as synonyms, antonyms, idioms, one-word substitution and spelling. Revise subject–verb agreement, tenses, prepositions, commonly confused words (their/there) and use of adverbs. In passages, answer only from what is stated. Daily reading of a newspaper and noting new words is the most reliable way to improve speed and accuracy.
questions:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Sunita, a farmer near Nashik, used to borrow from a local moneylender who charged very high interest. After she joined a self-help group, she could take small loans at a much lower rate and repay them in easy instalments. Within two years she bought a water pump and her onion yield nearly doubled.
What helped Sunita get loans at a lower rate of interest?
Joining a self-help group
Selling her onion crop early
Borrowing from the moneylender
Buying a new water pump
The passage says that after she joined a self-help group she could take small loans at a much lower rate. The moneylender charged high interest, and the pump was bought later with the loan.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Sunita, a farmer near Nashik, used to borrow from a local moneylender who charged very high interest. After she joined a self-help group, she could take small loans at a much lower rate and repay them in easy instalments. Within two years she bought a water pump and her onion yield nearly doubled.
Which of the following best describes what the passage is mainly about?
Why moneylenders charge very high interest
How onions are grown in Nashik district
Why farmers should avoid all kinds of loans
How cheaper credit improved a farmer's life
The passage traces Sunita's move from costly moneylender loans to cheaper group loans and the resulting rise in her yield. Its focus is on how affordable credit improved her livelihood.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Sunita, a farmer near Nashik, used to borrow from a local moneylender who charged very high interest. After she joined a self-help group, she could take small loans at a much lower rate and repay them in easy instalments. Within two years she bought a water pump and her onion yield nearly doubled.
As used in the passage, the word 'yield' most nearly means:
Surrender
Profit share
Output
Interest
In farming, 'yield' means the amount of crop produced, that is the output. 'Surrender' is another meaning of the verb 'yield', but it does not fit the context of onion harvests.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
Please ________ the account-opening form in capital letters.
fall
fill
feel
fell
One fills (in) a form, so 'fill' is correct. 'Fall', 'feel' and 'fell' are similar-sounding words but make no sense with 'the account-opening form'.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The cashier counted the notes ________ before handing them over to the customer.
carefully
careful
care
careless
The blank describes how the cashier counted, so an adverb is needed: 'carefully'. 'Careful' is an adjective and 'care' is a noun; 'careless' is an adjective with the opposite sense.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The loan amount will be credited ________ your savings account within two working days.
at
of
by
to
Money is credited to an account, so 'to' is the correct preposition. 'At', 'of' and 'by' do not combine with 'credited' to show the destination of the money.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
My brother and I (A) / goes to the bank (B) / every Saturday (C) / to deposit money. (D)
Two subjects joined by 'and' (My brother and I) take a plural verb. So 'goes' must be 'go'. The error lies in part (B); the other parts are correct.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The news (A) / about the merger (B) / were announced (C) / yesterday morning. (D)
'News' looks plural but is an uncountable singular noun, so it takes 'was': 'The news was announced'. The error is in part (C).

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
All the customers were (A) / asked to stand (B) / in a queue and (C) / wait for there turn. (D)
'There' is an adverb of place; the possessive pronoun needed here is 'their', as in 'wait for their turn'. So part (D) contains the error.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
If it rains tomorrow, we WILL STAYED at home.
will stay
would stayed
will staying
No improvement required
After the modal 'will', the base form of the verb is used: 'will stay'. In a first conditional, the if-clause takes simple present (rains) and the main clause takes 'will' + base verb.

Rearrange the sentences to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: First, she took a withdrawal slip from the counter and filled it in.
Q: Asha reached the bank at ten in the morning.
R: After checking her signature, the cashier gave her the cash.
S: Then she stood in the queue and handed the slip to the cashier.
QSPR
PQSR
QPSR
QPRS
Q opens with Asha arriving, P begins the process with 'First', S follows with 'Then', and R ends with the cashier paying her. The time words fix the order as QPSR.
Select the word that means the same as GENUINE.
Fake
Authentic
Rude
Fragile
Genuine means real or truly what it is said to be, so 'authentic' is the synonym. 'Fake' is its antonym, and rude or fragile are unrelated in meaning.
Pick the antonym of EXPAND.
Contract
Extend
Enlarge
Spread
To expand is to become larger. 'Contract' means to become smaller, so it is the opposite. Extend, enlarge and spread are all close in meaning to expand.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To turn over a new leaf'.
To start reading a new book
To plant trees in a new garden
To move to a new house or city
To change one's behaviour for the better
'Turn over a new leaf' means to make a fresh start by improving one's conduct or habits. The literal readings about books, plants or houses are traps.
Choose the one word for: 'A list of items to be discussed at a meeting'.
Minutes
Memo
Agenda
Notice
An agenda lists the topics to be taken up at a meeting. Minutes are the written record of what was discussed afterwards, a common confusion, while a memo or notice is a general communication.

Numerical Ability.overview: Numerical Ability covers simplification and approximation, number series, quadratic equations, and arithmetic: percentages, profit and loss with discount, simple and compound interest, ratio and proportion, averages, ages, time and work, speed and distance, mensuration, probability and simple data interpretation. Speed matters as much as accuracy, so learn squares up to 30, cubes up to 20, and percentage–fraction equivalents. Use BODMAS correctly and approximate smartly. Practise mixed sets under time pressure to decide which questions to attempt first.
questions:
What will come in place of the question mark (?)
45% of 640 + 15² − 18 × 7 = ?
45% of 640 = 288, 15² = 225 and 18 × 7 = 126. So 288 + 225 − 126 = 387. Follow BODMAS: finish percentage, square and product before adding and subtracting.

What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?)
24.98 × 12.03 + 299.97 ÷ 6.02 = ?
Round each number: 25 × 12 = 300 and 300 ÷ 6 = 50. The total is about 300 + 50 = 350. Division is done before addition, as BODMAS requires.

What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the series?
2, 6, 15, 31, 56, ?
The differences are 4, 9, 16, 25, which are squares of 2, 3, 4, 5. The next difference is 6² = 36, so the missing term is 56 + 36 = 92.

Find the roots of each quadratic below and decide how x relates to y.
I. x² + 5x + 6 = 0
II. y² + 7y + 12 = 0
x > y
x ≥ y
x ≤ y
Relationship cannot be established
I gives x = −2 or −3; II gives y = −3 or −4. Every x is greater than or equal to every y, and x = y = −3 is possible, so x ≥ y. Watch the signs with negative roots.
A student scored 36% marks and failed by 18 marks. If the pass mark is 45%, what are the maximum marks of the exam?
The gap between the pass mark and the student's score is 45% − 36% = 9% of the maximum marks, which equals 18 marks. So maximum marks = 18 ÷ 0.09 = 200.
The marked price of a ceiling fan is ₹2,000. The shopkeeper allows a 10% discount and still makes a 20% profit. What is the cost price of the fan?
Selling price = 90% of 2,000 = ₹1,800. This includes a 20% profit, so cost price = 1,800 ÷ 1.2 = ₹1,500. Taking 20% off ₹1,800 gives ₹1,440, a common error.
At simple interest, a sum of money amounts to ₹7,200 in 2 years and to ₹8,400 in 4 years. What is the rate of interest per annum?
The extra ₹1,200 over 2 years means SI of ₹600 per year. Principal = 7,200 − 2 × 600 = ₹6,000. Rate = 600 ÷ 6,000 × 100 = 10% per annum.
An amount of ₹1,350 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is C's share?
Total parts = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9, so one part is 1,350 ÷ 9 = ₹150. C gets 4 parts = ₹600. ₹450 is B's share and ₹300 is A's share.
The average age of 30 students in a class is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises by 1 year. What is the teacher's age?
45 years
44 years
46 years
40 years
Total age of students = 30 × 14 = 420. With the teacher, total = 31 × 15 = 465. Teacher's age = 465 − 420 = 45 years.
The sum of the present ages of a mother and her daughter is 50 years. Five years ago, the mother was seven times as old as the daughter. What is the mother's present age?
35 years
42 years
38 years
40 years
Let the daughter be d; mother = 50 − d. Then 45 − d = 7(d − 5), so 8d = 80 and d = 10. Mother is 40 years old. Check: five years ago 35 = 7 × 5.
A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B in 30 days. A works alone for 10 days and then leaves. In how many days will B finish the remaining work?
12 days
18 days
15 days
10 days
In 10 days A completes 10/20 = half the work. B does 1/30 per day, so the remaining half takes 30 × 1/2 = 15 days.
A car covers a certain distance at 60 km/h in 5 hours. At what speed must it travel to cover the same distance in 4 hours?
70 km/h
75 km/h
80 km/h
72 km/h
Distance = 60 × 5 = 300 km. To cover 300 km in 4 hours, speed = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 km/h. Speed and time are inversely proportional for a fixed distance.
The area of a rectangular plot is 432 m² and its length is 24 m. What is the perimeter of the plot?
Breadth = 432 ÷ 24 = 18 m. Perimeter = 2 × (24 + 18) = 84 m. Remember to add length and breadth before doubling, not just to double one side.
One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king or a heart?
There are 13 hearts and 4 kings, but the king of hearts is counted twice. Favourable cards = 13 + 4 − 1 = 16, so P = 16/52 = 4/13. Not subtracting the overlap gives 17/52.

The number of savings accounts opened by a bank branch on five days of a week was:
Monday – 45, Tuesday – 60, Wednesday – 38, Thursday – 52, Friday – 55
What is the average number of accounts opened per day?
Total accounts = 45 + 60 + 38 + 52 + 55 = 250. Average = 250 ÷ 5 = 50 accounts per day. Add carefully before dividing; one slip in the total changes the answer.

Reasoning Ability.overview: Reasoning for IBPS Clerk includes linear seating, box and day-based puzzles, syllogisms, inequalities, blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding, ranking, alphabet tests, odd one out and series. Puzzles are usually simpler than in PO but still take time, so draw neat diagrams and fix definite positions first. For syllogisms learn the 'either–or' case and complementary pairs. In coding, look for patterns such as opposite letters, shifts and letter-position values. Regular timed practice builds the speed this section needs.
questions:
Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north.
• B sits second from the left end.
• Only one person sits between B and D.
• E sits immediately to the right of D.
• A does not sit at either end.
Who sits at the extreme left end?
A
C
E
B
B is 2nd, so D is 4th (there is no position 0). E is immediately right of D, so 5th. A cannot be at an end, so A is 3rd and C takes the left end: C B A D E.

Six boxes P, Q, R, S, T and U are placed one above another.
• U is at the bottom.
• Only two boxes are placed between U and Q.
• Q is immediately above T.
• P is immediately above Q.
• R is placed somewhere above S.
Which box is at the top?
P
S
Q
R
U is 1st from bottom, so Q is 4th and T 3rd. P is 5th. R and S fill positions 2 and 6, and R must be above S, so R is on top (6th) and S is 2nd.

Five officers V, W, X, Y and Z visit a branch on different days from Monday to Friday.
• X visits on Wednesday.
• W visits on the day immediately after Y.
• Z visits on a day before X.
• V does not visit on Monday.
Who visits on Monday?
V
Y
W
Z
Y–W must be Monday–Tuesday or Thursday–Friday. If Monday–Tuesday, Z has no day before Wednesday, so Y–W are Thursday–Friday. V cannot take Monday, so V is Tuesday and Z is Monday.

Statements: All banks are buildings. No building is a tent.
Conclusions: I. No bank is a tent. II. Some buildings are banks.
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Banks lie wholly inside buildings, and buildings share nothing with tents, so no bank can be a tent. Since all banks are buildings, some buildings are certainly banks. Both conclusions follow.

Statements: Some cups are plates. Some plates are spoons.
Conclusions: I. Some cups are spoons. II. No cup is a spoon.
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Either I or II follows
Neither I nor II follows
Neither conclusion is certain on its own. But I and II form a complementary pair about the same two terms: one of them must always be true. Hence either I or II follows.

In the following question, the relationship between different elements is shown. Decide which conclusion(s) definitely hold true.
Given: R > S ≥ T ≥ U
Conclusions: I. R > U  II. S > U
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
R > S ≥ T ≥ U gives R > U because one strict sign is present, so I follows. Between S and U all signs are ≥, so S may equal U; II is not definite. Only I follows.
A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. D is the husband of C. How is A related to D?
Son
Nephew
Brother
Grandson
B is C's daughter, and A is B's brother, so A is C's son. D is C's husband, so D is A's father. Hence A is D's son.
Neha's mother is the sister of Ravi's father. How is Ravi related to Neha?
Brother
Cousin
Nephew
Uncle
Neha's mother and Ravi's father are siblings. Children of siblings are cousins, so Ravi is Neha's cousin. He cannot be her brother because they have different parents.
Mohan walks 15 m towards north, turns right and walks 8 m, then turns right again and walks 9 m. How far is he from his starting point?
8 m
North 15 m, then right (east) 8 m, then right again (south) 9 m. He is 15 − 9 = 6 m north and 8 m east of the start. Distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 m.
In a certain code, BANK is written as YZMP. How is CASH written in that code?
XZGS
DBTI
XAHS
XZHS
Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, N↔M, K↔P). For CASH: C→X, A→Z, S→H, H→S, giving XZHS.
If BAG is coded as 14 (the product of the positions of its letters in the alphabet), what is the code for DEAF?
B, A, G are 2, 1, 7 and 2 × 1 × 7 = 14. For DEAF, the positions are 4, 5, 1, 6, so the product is 4 × 5 × 1 × 6 = 120. The sum, 16, is a trap.
In a class of 35 students, Arun ranks 8th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
27th
28th
29th
26th
Rank from bottom = total − rank from top + 1 = 35 − 8 + 1 = 28th. Forgetting to add 1 gives 27th, a common slip.
Which letter of the English alphabet is 5th to the left of the 16th letter from the left end?
K
U
L
J
The 16th letter from the left is P. Moving 5 places to its left gives the 11th letter, K. Moving to the right instead would give U.

Find the odd one out:
121, 169, 225, 289, 323
121, 169, 225 and 289 are squares of 11, 13, 15 and 17. 323 is not a perfect square (it is 17 × 19), so it is the odd one out.

Find the wrong number in the series:
2, 5, 11, 23, 48, 95
Each term is double the previous term plus 1: 2, 5, 11, 23, 47, 95. So 48 should be 47. Note that 95 = 47 × 2 + 1, which confirms 48 is the wrong term.

English Language.overview: The English section of SBI PO prelims and mains tests reading comprehension, vocabulary in context, grammar and sentence structure. Expect passages on banking, economy and social issues followed by inference and tone questions, plus error spotting, fillers, para jumbles, sentence improvement and word usage. Focus on subject–verb agreement, conditionals, fixed conjunction pairs and connectors, and build vocabulary through regular reading of editorials. In comprehension, answer only from what the passage states or clearly implies, and eliminate options that are too extreme or bring in outside information.
questions:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.
Many first-time borrowers in small towns now take loans through mobile apps. The speed is welcome, but some apps hide charges in fine print and use aggressive recovery methods. Regulators have responded by requiring lenders to disclose the full annual cost of a loan upfront. Experts say disclosure helps, yet borrowers also need basic financial literacy to compare offers sensibly.

What is the central concern raised in the passage?
Fast digital loans can harm borrowers who do not understand their true cost
Mobile apps have made banks in small towns completely unnecessary
Regulators have banned digital lenders from operating in small towns
Borrowers in small towns prefer slow loans from moneylenders

The passage welcomes speed but warns of hidden charges and harsh recovery, then stresses disclosure and literacy. Nothing says banks are unnecessary or that lending is banned, so only the first statement captures its central concern.

Read the passage and answer the question that follows.
Many first-time borrowers in small towns now take loans through mobile apps. The speed is welcome, but some apps hide charges in fine print and use aggressive recovery methods. Regulators have responded by requiring lenders to disclose the full annual cost of a loan upfront. Experts say disclosure helps, yet borrowers also need basic financial literacy to compare offers sensibly.

According to the passage, why is disclosure alone considered insufficient?
Lenders can easily ignore the disclosure requirement
The annual cost of a loan cannot be calculated in advance
Mobile apps do not allow lenders to display any charges
Borrowers must also be able to compare loan offers sensibly
The last sentence says disclosure helps, yet borrowers also need financial literacy to compare offers. The passage does not claim lenders ignore the rule or that costs cannot be calculated.

Read the passage and answer the question that follows.
Many first-time borrowers in small towns now take loans through mobile apps. The speed is welcome, but some apps hide charges in fine print and use aggressive recovery methods. Regulators have responded by requiring lenders to disclose the full annual cost of a loan upfront. Experts say disclosure helps, yet borrowers also need basic financial literacy to compare offers sensibly.

Which word is closest in meaning to 'aggressive' as used in the passage?
Generous
Delayed
Careless
Forceful
'Aggressive recovery methods' means pushy, forceful ways of collecting dues. 'Generous' is nearly opposite, while 'delayed' and 'careless' do not describe the pressure the passage is criticising.

Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.
Despite several reminders from the branch, the borrower remained ________ about repaying the overdue amount.
punctual
indifferent
diligent
eager

'Despite several reminders' signals that the borrower did not care, so 'indifferent' fits. 'Punctual', 'diligent' and 'eager' would all suggest willingness to repay, which contradicts the contrast set up by 'despite'.

Select the pair of words that fits both blanks correctly.
The committee's report was ________ by the board, which promptly ________ most of its recommendations.
endorsed, adopted
rejected, adopted
ignored, implemented
endorsed, discarded

A board that approves a report would logically adopt its recommendations, so 'endorsed, adopted' is consistent. The other pairs contradict each other, for example rejecting a report and then adopting its recommendations.

Find the part of the sentence that has a grammatical error.
Each of the applicants (A) / have been asked (B) / to submit (C) / the documents by Friday. (D)
The subject is 'Each', which is singular, so the verb must be 'has been asked', not 'have been asked'. The phrase 'of the applicants' does not change the number of the subject.

Find the part of the sentence that has a grammatical error.
Hardly had the auditors (A) / entered the branch (B) / than the manager (C) / produced all the ledgers. (D)

'Hardly' and 'scarcely' are followed by 'when', not 'than'. The correct form is 'Hardly had the auditors entered the branch when the manager produced all the ledgers'. 'No sooner' is the phrase that takes 'than'.

Find the part of the sentence that has a grammatical error.
The volume of digital payments (A) / in rural districts (B) / have risen steadily (C) / over the last five years. (D)
The head noun of the subject is 'volume', which is singular, so the verb should be 'has risen'. The plural 'payments' and 'districts' are inside prepositional phrases and do not decide the verb.

Improve the part in capitals, if needed.
If I WOULD HAVE KNOWN about the deadline, I would have applied much earlier.
had known
would know
have known
No improvement required
In a third conditional the if-clause takes the past perfect: 'If I had known…, I would have applied'. 'Would have' should appear only in the main clause, so the sentence needs correction.

Arrange the sentences P, Q, R and S in a logical order.
P: As a result, the branch decided to open on Saturdays as well.
Q: Footfall at the new branch was far higher than expected.
R: The extra day reduced waiting time considerably.
S: Long queues began forming on weekdays.
SQPR
QPSR
QSRP
QSPR

Q introduces high footfall, S states its effect (long queues), P gives the response ('As a result', Saturday opening) and R reports the outcome of that extra day. Other orders place the result before its cause.
In the sentence 'A prudent lender checks the repayment capacity of every borrower', which word can replace PRUDENT without changing the meaning?
Reckless
Generous
Judicious
Hasty
'Prudent' means acting with care and good judgement, which matches 'judicious'. 'Reckless' and 'hasty' are near opposites, and 'generous' refers to willingness to give rather than careful judgement.
Pick the word that is the opposite of FRUGAL.
Economical
Extravagant
Thrifty
Careful

'Frugal' describes someone who spends sparingly. Its opposite is 'extravagant', meaning spending lavishly. 'Economical' and 'thrifty' are synonyms of frugal, and 'careful' is close in meaning, not opposite.
What does the idiom 'a red herring' mean in the sentence: 'The rumour about a merger was a red herring during the audit'?
Something that distracts attention from the real issue
A financial loss that is hidden in the accounts
A warning sign that predicts an approaching crisis
A rare opportunity that must be grabbed at once

A red herring is a misleading clue that draws attention away from the actual matter. It does not refer to a hidden loss, a warning sign or an opportunity, though these may sound related in a banking context.
Choose the single word for: 'A form of government in which power rests with a small group of people'.
Monarchy
Democracy
Anarchy
Oligarchy
Oligarchy means rule by a few. Monarchy is rule by one sovereign, democracy is rule by the people through elected representatives, and anarchy is the absence of any government authority.

Choose the connector that best fits the blank.
The pilot project earned steady profits for two years; ________, the board approved its expansion to fifty more branches.
nevertheless
otherwise
consequently
meanwhile

Profits leading to approval of expansion is a cause-and-effect link, so 'consequently' fits. 'Nevertheless' signals contrast, 'otherwise' signals an alternative condition and 'meanwhile' signals simultaneous events, none of which suit this logic.

Quantitative Aptitude.overview: Quantitative Aptitude for SBI PO covers simplification and approximation, number series, quadratic equations, arithmetic word problems (percentage, profit and loss, interest, ratio, partnership, time and work, speed and distance, mixtures), probability, permutations and combinations, mensuration and data interpretation. Mains adds caselets and data sufficiency. Learn shortcuts such as CI − SI for two years and harmonic-mean average speed, but always check units and time periods. Practise DI sets under time pressure and approximate wherever options are far apart.
questions:
Find the value of ?
35% of 840 + 2/3 of 432 = ?

35% of 840 = 294 and two-thirds of 432 = 288. Adding them gives 294 + 288 = 582. Computing percentages and fractions separately before adding avoids most calculation slips in simplification questions.
Find the next term of the series: 3, 7, 16, 32, 57, ?
The differences are 4, 9, 16 and 25, which are squares of 2, 3, 4 and 5. The next difference is 6² = 36, so the next term is 57 + 36 = 93.

One number in the series below does not follow the pattern. Identify it.
2, 5, 11, 23, 47, 96, 191
Each term is twice the previous term plus 1: 2→5→11→23→47→95→191. So 96 is wrong and should be 95. Note that 191 = 2 × 95 + 1 also confirms the pattern.

Solve the two equations and find the relationship between x and y.
I. x² − 11x + 30 = 0
II. y² − 13y + 42 = 0
x > y
x < y
x ≤ y
x ≥ y
From I, x = 5 or 6. From II, y = 6 or 7. Every x is less than or equal to every y, and the case x = y = 6 rules out the strict relation x < y. Hence x ≤ y.
A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
Take cost price as 100. Marked price = 140 and selling price = 140 × 0.85 = 119. Profit = 19 on 100, i.e. 19%. Simply subtracting 15 from 40 to get 25% is a common error.
The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹96. What is the sum?
For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (r/100)². So 96 = P × 0.0064, giving P = ₹15,000. This shortcut works only for a two-year period with annual compounding.
A starts a business with ₹24,000. Five months later B joins with ₹36,000. At the end of the year the profit is ₹30,000. What is B's share?
Capital-time: A = 24,000 × 12 = 2,88,000; B = 36,000 × 7 = 2,52,000. Ratio 8 : 7. B's share = 30,000 × 7/15 = ₹14,000. Forgetting that B invested for only 7 months gives wrong options.
A can finish a task in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 6 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining task?
12 days
18 days
15 days
10 days
Together they do 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 per day, so in 6 days they finish half the task. B alone needs 30 × 1/2 = 15 days for the remaining half.
A car travels from town X to town Y at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
50 km/h
48 km/h
45 km/h
52 km/h
For equal distances, average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 60 × 40/100 = 48 km/h. The simple average of 50 km/h is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed.
A train running at 72 km/h passes a signal pole in 15 seconds and crosses a platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
72 km/h = 20 m/s. Train length = 20 × 15 = 300 m. Crossing the platform covers 20 × 25 = 500 m, so the platform is 500 − 300 = 200 m. The 300 m option is the train itself.
A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 5 : 3. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1 : 1?
8 litres
12 litres
15 litres
10 litres
Milk = 25 litres and water = 15 litres. For a 1 : 1 ratio, water must equal milk, i.e. 25 litres, so 25 − 15 = 10 litres of water must be added.
A bag has 4 red, 5 blue and 3 green balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that both are of the same colour?
Total ways = 12C2 = 66. Same colour: 4C2 + 5C2 + 3C2 = 6 + 10 + 3 = 19. Probability = 19/66. Leaving out the green pair gives 16/66, a common slip.
In how many ways can the letters of the word BANKER be arranged so that the vowels always come together?
The vowels A and E form one unit, giving 5 units that can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways. The vowels can swap among themselves in 2 ways, so the total is 120 × 2 = 240.

Deposits (₹ crore) of three branches are given.
Branch P: 2023 – 240, 2024 – 300
Branch Q: 2023 – 180, 2024 – 210
Branch R: 2023 – 280, 2024 – 340
What is the approximate percentage increase in the combined deposits of the three branches from 2023 to 2024?
Combined deposits rise from 700 to 850 crore, an increase of 150. Percentage increase = 150/700 × 100 ≈ 21.4%. Branch P alone grew 25%, which is a distractor, not the combined figure.
The length of a rectangular hall is increased by 20% and its breadth is decreased by 20%. What is the effect on its area?
No change
Increases by 4%
Decreases by 2%
Decreases by 4%
New area = 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 of the original, a 4% decrease. Equal percentage increase and decrease never cancel out; the net effect is always a fall of x²/100 per cent.

Reasoning Ability.overview: Reasoning Ability for SBI PO tests puzzles and seating arrangements (linear, circular, floor-based), syllogisms including possibility cases, coded and direct inequalities, blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding, ranking and alphanumeric series. Mains adds input-output and logical reasoning such as assumptions and courses of action. Draw neat diagrams, fix definite clues first and test each remaining case. In syllogisms use Venn diagrams and treat 'possibility' conclusions separately. In inequalities, a conclusion follows only when it is definitely true.
questions:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F live on the six floors of a building, one on each floor. The lowest floor is numbered 1 and the top floor 6.
• C lives on an even-numbered floor above D.
• Exactly two persons live between C and F.
• A lives immediately above F.
• D lives on an even-numbered floor, immediately above E.
• B does not live on the top floor.

Who lives on the floor immediately below B?
C
F
A
D
C must be on 6 (an even floor above an even floor D with E below it). Then F is on 3, A on 4, D on 2 and E on 1, leaving B on 5. A is directly below B.

Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F live on the six floors of a building, one on each floor. The lowest floor is numbered 1 and the top floor 6.
• C lives on an even-numbered floor above D.
• Exactly two persons live between C and F.
• A lives immediately above F.
• D lives on an even-numbered floor, immediately above E.
• B does not live on the top floor.

How many persons live between E and A?
One
Two
Three
None
The arrangement from bottom is E(1), D(2), F(3), A(4), B(5), C(6). Between E on floor 1 and A on floor 4 are D and F, so two persons live between them.

Five persons P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north.
• R sits exactly in the middle.
• Q sits at one of the extreme ends.
• S sits second to the left of R.
• T does not sit next to Q.

Who sits immediately to the left of Q?
P
T
S
R
R is 3rd, so S is 1st. Q must then be at the right end (5th). T cannot be next to Q, so T is 2nd and P is 4th, immediately to the left of Q.

Statements: All banks are buildings. Some buildings are offices. No office is a shop.
Conclusions: I. Some banks are offices. II. Some buildings are not shops.
Only conclusion I follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Only conclusion II follows
The buildings that are offices cannot be shops, so some buildings are definitely not shops (II follows). Banks may or may not overlap with offices, so I is only a possibility and does not follow.

Statements: Some pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are not erasers. II. All erasers being pens is a possibility.
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Pens that are pencils can never be erasers, so I follows. Erasers can lie wholly inside the pen circle as long as they avoid the pencil region, so II is a valid possibility. Both follow.

Statements: P ≥ Q > R = S; T < S ≤ U
Conclusions: I. P > T  II. U ≥ R
Only conclusion I follows
Both I and II follow
Only conclusion II follows
Neither I nor II follows
Combining, P ≥ Q > R = S > T gives P > T, so I is true. Also U ≥ S = R gives U ≥ R, so II is true. Both conclusions follow.

Statements: A > B ≥ C; D ≤ C < E; F = E
Conclusions: I. F > D  II. B > D
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
F = E > C ≥ D gives F > D, so I follows. For II, B ≥ C ≥ D only gives B ≥ D; B could equal D, so B > D is not certain. Only I follows.
Pointing to a young man, Kavya said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the young man related to Kavya?
Nephew
Brother
Cousin
Son
Kavya is a woman, so the only daughter of her mother is Kavya herself. The young man's mother is therefore Kavya, making him her son. 'Nephew' would require a sister, which the clue rules out.

A + B means A is the father of B; A − B means A is the wife of B; A × B means A is the brother of B; A ÷ B means A is the daughter of B.
If P ÷ Q − R × S, how is R related to P?
Uncle
Brother
Father
Grandfather
P is the daughter of Q, and Q is the wife of R, so R is P's father. R × S only tells us R is S's brother, making S P's uncle or aunt, not changing R's relation.
Manoj walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 6 m, turns right again and walks 18 m, then turns left and walks 9 m. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
15 m, South-East
17 m, South-East
17 m, North-East
13 m, South-West
Net movement: east 6 + 9 = 15 m and south 18 − 10 = 8 m. Distance = √(15² + 8²) = 17 m. Being east and south of the start, he is to the South-East.
In a certain code, PLANT is written as QNDRY. How is SAVER written in that code?
TCYIW
TBYIV
TCXIW
UCYIW
The letters are shifted forward by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 places in order: P+1=Q, L+2=N, A+3=D, N+4=R, T+5=Y. Applying the same to SAVER gives T, C, Y, I, W.
In a secret language, 'loan is approved' is coded 'ka zo ri', 'approved by manager' is coded 'zo lu pe' and 'manager is busy' is coded 'pe ka mi'. Which code stands for 'by'?
zo
pe
ri
lu
'approved' = zo (common to first two), 'manager' = pe (common to last two) and 'is' = ka. In 'approved by manager', the remaining code lu must mean 'by'. 'ri' stands for 'loan'.
In a row of students, Asha is 12th from the left and Bina is 18th from the right. When they exchange places, Asha becomes 20th from the left. How many students are in the row?
After exchanging, Asha occupies Bina's old seat, which is 20th from the left and 18th from the right. Total = 20 + 18 − 1 = 37. Asha's original position is not needed.

Study the sequence: M 3 # K 8 R @ 5 T % 2 Q 9 & L
How many symbols are immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a letter?
One
Two
Three
Four
Check each symbol: '#' has 3 before and K after (counts); '@' has R before; '%' has T before; '&' has 9 before and L after (counts). So exactly two symbols meet the condition.
If the letters of the word BRANDS are arranged in alphabetical order, how many letters will remain in the same position?
Two
One
Three
None
Alphabetical order gives A B D N R S. Comparing with B R A N D S position by position, only N (4th) and S (6th) stay unchanged, so two letters remain in place.

English Language.overview: The English Language section of SBI Clerk (Junior Associate) checks basic grammar, vocabulary and reading skills. Expect short comprehension passages, fillers, error spotting, sentence improvement, para jumbles, synonyms and antonyms, idioms, spellings and one-word substitution. Revise subject–verb agreement, tenses, prepositions of time, and common errors such as redundancy ('return back') and 'one of' with plural nouns. Read passages carefully and pick answers stated in the text rather than from general knowledge. Accuracy matters because of negative marking.
questions:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.
Lakshmi runs a small tailoring shop in her village. For years she kept her earnings in a tin box at home. Last year a bank correspondent visited the village and helped her open a savings account using her Aadhaar card. Now she deposits money every week and has also started a small recurring deposit for her daughter's education. She says the account has given her both safety and discipline.

Where did Lakshmi keep her earnings before she opened the account?
With a local moneylender
In a tin box at home
In her daughter's school
In a post office account
The passage clearly says that for years she kept her earnings in a tin box at home. A moneylender, school or post office is never mentioned, so those options are unsupported.

Read the passage and answer the question that follows.
Lakshmi runs a small tailoring shop in her village. For years she kept her earnings in a tin box at home. Last year a bank correspondent visited the village and helped her open a savings account using her Aadhaar card. Now she deposits money every week and has also started a small recurring deposit for her daughter's education. She says the account has given her both safety and discipline.

Why has Lakshmi started a recurring deposit?
To buy new machines for her tailoring shop
To repay a loan taken from the bank
To pay the bank correspondent's fee
To save for her daughter's education
The passage states that she started a small recurring deposit for her daughter's education. Shop machines, loan repayment and fees are not mentioned anywhere, so these options are distractors.

Read the passage and answer the question that follows.
Lakshmi runs a small tailoring shop in her village. For years she kept her earnings in a tin box at home. Last year a bank correspondent visited the village and helped her open a savings account using her Aadhaar card. Now she deposits money every week and has also started a small recurring deposit for her daughter's education. She says the account has given her both safety and discipline.

Which word is closest in meaning to 'discipline' as used in the passage?
Punishment
Freedom
Regularity
Confusion

Here 'discipline' refers to the habit of saving money every week in a regular, controlled way. 'Punishment' is another meaning of the word but does not fit this context; 'freedom' and 'confusion' do not fit at all.

Fill in the blank with the correct word.
Mr. Sharma has been working at this branch ________ five years.
since
for
from
by
'For' is used with a period of time (five years), while 'since' is used with a point of time (since 2020). 'From' and 'by' do not fit with the present perfect continuous here.

Fill in the blank with the correct verb form.
Neither the manager nor the clerks ________ present at yesterday's meeting.
was
is
has been
were
With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject 'clerks' is plural, and 'yesterday' needs the past tense, so 'were' is correct, not 'was'.

Which part of the sentence contains an error?
She don't know (A) / how to fill (B) / the deposit slip (C) / correctly. (D)
The subject 'She' is third-person singular, so the correct form is 'She doesn't know', not 'She don't know'. The rest of the sentence is grammatically correct.

Which part of the sentence contains an error?
The cashier (A) / gave me (B) / a ten-rupees note (C) / as change. (D)
When a number and a noun together act as an adjective before another noun, the noun stays singular: 'a ten-rupee note'. Hence 'ten-rupees' in part (C) is wrong.

Which part of the sentence contains an error?
One of my friend (A) / has opened (B) / a savings account (C) / in this bank. (D)
'One of' is always followed by a plural noun, so it should be 'One of my friends'. The verb 'has opened' is correct because the subject 'One' is singular.

Improve the part in capitals, if needed.
After signing the form, he RETURNED BACK it to the officer.
returned
returned again
had return back
No improvement required
'Return' already means to give or go back, so 'returned back' is redundant. The correct sentence is 'he returned it to the officer'. 'Had return back' is also ungrammatical.

Arrange the sentences P, Q, R and S in a logical order.
P: He filled in the withdrawal form carefully.
Q: Amit went to the bank to withdraw some cash.
R: Finally, the cashier handed him the money.
S: He then submitted the form at the counter.
QSPR
PQSR
QPRS
QPSR
Q introduces Amit going to the bank, P describes filling the form, S ('then') shows him submitting it and R ('Finally') ends with receiving the cash. This is the only natural sequence.
Select the word that means the same as ABUNDANT.
Scarce
Expensive
Plentiful
Hidden
'Abundant' means available in large quantities, which matches 'plentiful'. 'Scarce' is its opposite, while 'expensive' and 'hidden' are unrelated to quantity.
Select the word that is the opposite of ANCIENT.
Old
Modern
Historic
Antique
'Ancient' means belonging to the very distant past. Its opposite is 'modern'. 'Old', 'historic' and 'antique' all carry a sense of age, so they are similar in meaning, not opposite.
What does the idiom 'to break the ice' mean?
To start a conversation in an awkward situation
To cause serious damage to something
To end a long friendship suddenly
To complete a difficult task quickly
'To break the ice' means to say or do something that eases tension and starts a conversation, for example among strangers. It has nothing to do with damage, ending friendships or finishing tasks.
Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
Comittee
Commitee
Comitee
Committee
The correct spelling has double 'm', double 't' and double 'e': C-O-M-M-I-T-T-E-E. Each wrong option drops one of these doubled letters, a frequent spelling error in exams.
Give one word for: 'A person who travels on foot along a road'.
Passenger
Pilgrim
Pedestrian
Commuter
A pedestrian is a person walking on a road. A passenger travels in a vehicle, a pilgrim travels to a holy place, and a commuter travels regularly between home and work, usually by vehicle.

Numerical Ability.overview: Numerical Ability in SBI Clerk covers simplification and approximation, number series, percentages, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, ratio and proportion, averages, ages, time and work, speed and distance, mensuration and basic data interpretation. Most questions are calculation-heavy rather than tricky, so speed is key. Memorise squares, cubes and fraction–percentage equivalents, practise BODMAS carefully and learn standard formulas such as the half-yearly compounding rule. In DI, find totals first and then calculate shares or growth.
questions:
Find the value of ?
48 ÷ 6 × 9 − 25 + 7² = ?
Following BODMAS: 7² = 49, then 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 8 × 9 = 72. Finally 72 − 25 + 49 = 96. Division and multiplication are done left to right before addition and subtraction.

Find the approximate value of ?
24.98% of 639.9 + 15.02 × 6.97 = ?
Round off: 25% of 640 = 160 and 15 × 7 = 105. Adding gives 160 + 105 = 265. Rounding each value to the nearest convenient number keeps the error very small.
Find the next term of the series: 7, 10, 16, 25, 37, ?
The differences are 3, 6, 9 and 12, increasing by 3 each time. The next difference is 15, so the next term is 37 + 15 = 52.
Find the next term of the series: 3, 6, 18, 72, 360, ?
Each term is multiplied by 2, 3, 4 and 5 in turn: 3×2=6, 6×3=18, 18×4=72, 72×5=360. The next multiplier is 6, so 360 × 6 = 2160.
Identify the number that does not fit the pattern: 1, 4, 9, 16, 26, 36
The series lists perfect squares: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², 6². The fifth term should be 25, so 26 is the wrong number. All other terms are correct squares.
Ravi's monthly salary of ₹25,000 is first increased by 10% and then the new salary is reduced by 10%. What is his final salary?
After the increase: 25,000 × 1.10 = 27,500. After the cut: 27,500 × 0.90 = 24,750. The 10% cut applies to a larger amount, so the salary does not return to ₹25,000.
A shopkeeper buys a fan for ₹450 and sells it for ₹540. What is his profit percentage?
Profit = 540 − 450 = ₹90. Profit percentage is calculated on cost price: 90/450 × 100 = 20%. Calculating on selling price would wrongly give 16.67%.
What simple interest will ₹6,000 earn in 3 years at 8% per annum?
Simple interest = P × R × T / 100 = 6,000 × 8 × 3 / 100 = ₹1,440. Interest is calculated only on the original principal each year.
Find the compound interest on ₹10,000 for 1 year at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly.
Half-yearly compounding means a rate of 5% for 2 periods. Amount = 10,000 × 1.05² = ₹11,025, so CI = ₹1,025. Annual compounding would give only ₹1,000.
₹1,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much does C receive?
Total parts = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. C's share = 1,800 × 4/9 = ₹800. B would get ₹600 and A ₹400, which together with C's share total ₹1,800.
The average of five numbers is 40. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 38. What number was removed?
Sum of five numbers = 5 × 40 = 200. Sum of four numbers = 4 × 38 = 152. The removed number = 200 − 152 = 48.
A 150 m long train is running at 54 km/h. How long will it take to pass an electric pole?
9 seconds
12 seconds
10 seconds
15 seconds
54 km/h × 5/18 = 15 m/s. To pass a pole, the train covers only its own length, so time = 150 / 15 = 10 seconds.
A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B in 24 days. In how many days can they finish it working together?
9 days
8 days
6 days
18 days
A does 1/12 and B does 1/24 of the work per day. Together: 1/12 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8, so they finish in 8 days. Averaging 12 and 24 to get 18 is wrong.
The present ages of two brothers are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 6 years the ratio will be 3 : 4. What is the present age of the elder brother?
42 years
35 years
28 years
48 years
Let ages be 5x and 7x. Then (5x + 6)/(7x + 6) = 3/4, so 20x + 24 = 21x + 18, giving x = 6. The elder brother is 7 × 6 = 42 years old.

Loans disbursed (₹ lakh) by four branches in a month: Branch A – 45, Branch B – 60, Branch C – 75, Branch D – 70.
What percentage of the total loans was disbursed by Branch C?
Total disbursement = 45 + 60 + 75 + 70 = ₹250 lakh. Branch C's share = 75/250 × 100 = 30%. Check that the total is right before finding any percentage share.

Reasoning Ability.overview: Reasoning Ability for SBI Clerk includes seating arrangements and simple puzzles, syllogisms, inequalities, blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding, ranking and ordering, alphabet and number analogies, and odd-one-out questions. Place fixed clues first in puzzles, then test the remaining cases. Draw family trees and direction diagrams instead of solving mentally, and use Venn diagrams for syllogisms. For inequalities, chain the relations and check whether a conclusion is definitely true. Regular timed practice builds speed for prelims.
questions:
Six persons J, K, L, M, N and O sit in a row facing north.
• M sits fourth from the left end.
• J sits second to the left of M.
• N sits at one of the extreme ends.
• K is an immediate neighbour of both M and N.
• O sits immediately to the right of J.

Who sits at the extreme left end?
N
J
L
O
M is 4th and J is 2nd. K must touch both M and N, so N is at the right end (6th) and K is 5th. O is 3rd, right of J, leaving L at the extreme left.

Six persons J, K, L, M, N and O sit in a row facing north.
• M sits fourth from the left end.
• J sits second to the left of M.
• N sits at one of the extreme ends.
• K is an immediate neighbour of both M and N.
• O sits immediately to the right of J.

How many persons sit between L and K?
Two
Three
Four
One
The final order from left is L, J, O, M, K, N. Between L (1st) and K (5th) sit J, O and M, which makes three persons.

Statements: All pens are books. Some books are bags.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are bags. II. Some books are pens.
Only conclusion II follows
Only conclusion I follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Since all pens are books, some books are definitely pens, so II follows. The bags that are books may lie outside the pen circle, so I is not certain.

Statements: No cup is a plate. All plates are bowls.
Conclusions: I. Some bowls are not cups. II. Some cups are bowls.
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Only conclusion I follows
The bowls that are plates can never be cups, so some bowls are not cups and I follows. Cups may or may not overlap with bowls outside the plate region, so II is not definite.

Statements: M ≥ N > O; O ≥ P; Q > M
Conclusions: I. Q > O  II. N > P
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Combining: Q > M ≥ N > O ≥ P. So Q > O is definitely true, and N > O ≥ P gives N > P. Both conclusions follow.
A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
Son
Grandson
Nephew
Granddaughter
A and B are children of C, and D is C's father. So A is D's grandchild; since A is a brother, A is D's grandson. 'Granddaughter' would fit B, not A.
Sunita walks 5 km towards the east, then turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance between her and the starting point?
13 km
17 km
12 km
15 km
Turning left from east means walking north. Her path forms a right angle, so the distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km. 17 km is the total distance walked, not the shortest.
A man is facing north. He turns 90° clockwise and then 135° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
North-East
South-West
West
North-West
After turning 90° clockwise he faces east. Turning 135° anticlockwise from east takes him past north by 45°, so he faces north-west. The net turn is 45° anticlockwise from north.
If MONEY is written as NPOFZ in a code, how will CHEQUE be written?
DIERVF
BGDPTD
DIFRVF
DIFRUF
Each letter is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet: M→N, O→P and so on. Applying this to CHEQUE gives D, I, F, R, V, F, i.e. DIFRVF.
If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3 and so on up to Z = 26, what is the total value of the word LOAN?
L = 12, O = 15, A = 1 and N = 14. Adding them: 12 + 15 + 1 + 14 = 42. Learning the positions of letters such as E, J, O, T and Y speeds up such questions.
Rohit is 15th from the top and 26th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in the class?
Total = position from top + position from bottom − 1 = 15 + 26 − 1 = 40. We subtract 1 because Rohit is counted in both positions.
Among five friends, P is taller than Q. R is shorter than Q but taller than S. T is the tallest of all. Who is the shortest?
R
Q
P
S
The order from tallest is T, P, Q, R, S. Since R is shorter than Q but taller than S, and no one else is placed below S, S is the shortest.
Which of these numbers is the odd one out: 27, 64, 144, 216?
27, 64 and 216 are perfect cubes (3³, 4³ and 6³). 144 is a perfect square (12²) but not a perfect cube, so it is the odd one out.
Complete the analogy: 6 : 35 :: 9 : ?
The rule is n² − 1: 6² − 1 = 35. Applying the same to 9 gives 81 − 1 = 80. The option 81 is only 9², missing the subtraction step.
Which letter is 7th to the right of the 15th letter from the left end of the English alphabet?
V
U
W
T
The 15th letter from the left is O. Moving 7 places to the right means 15 + 7 = 22nd letter, which is V.

General Awareness.overview: This section of RBI Grade B Phase I tests general awareness with a strong tilt towards banking and the economy. Expect questions on the RBI's history, functions and monetary policy tools, the liquidity adjustment framework, CRR and SLR, Basel III capital and liquidity norms, deposit insurance, development institutions such as NABARD, key constitutional provisions on public finance, and core macroeconomic ideas like the balance of payments, exchange rates and inequality. While revising, focus on stable concepts and the reasoning behind each tool, and cross-check any number-based fact against the latest RBI publications.
questions: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India nationalised, ending its status as a shareholders' bank?

The RBI began operations in 1935 as a privately held shareholders' bank and was nationalised with effect from 1 January 1949. The year 1969 is associated with the nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks, not the RBI.
When the RBI began operations in April 1935, where was its Central Office located before it moved permanently to Mumbai in 1937?
New Delhi
Calcutta (Kolkata)
Madras (Chennai)
Nagpur
The RBI's Central Office was first set up in Calcutta and shifted permanently to Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1937, where it remains, housing the Governor's office and policy departments.
The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) that banks must maintain is prescribed under which law?
Section 42 of the RBI Act, 1934
Section 17 of the RBI Act, 1934
Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
SLR is mandated by Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. Section 42 of the RBI Act, 1934 is the tempting distractor because it governs the Cash Reserve Ratio, not SLR.
Which liquidity tool lets the RBI absorb surplus funds from banks without having to give them government securities as collateral in return?
Standing Deposit Facility
Marginal Standing Facility
Fixed-rate reverse repo
Term repo auction

The Standing Deposit Facility absorbs liquidity without collateral, removing the constraint of the RBI's securities holdings. Reverse repo needs collateral, while MSF and term repo inject liquidity rather than absorb it.
A bank is checking which of its holdings count towards its SLR requirement. Which of the following would NOT qualify?
Rated bonds issued by a private manufacturing company
Cash held in its own vaults
Unencumbered Central Government securities
Gold valued as per RBI norms
SLR can be held in cash, gold and unencumbered approved securities such as Government securities. Corporate bonds, however safe or well rated, are not SLR-eligible assets.
Under Basel III norms, the Capital Conservation Buffer must be held in the form of:
Additional Tier 1 perpetual bonds
Common Equity Tier 1 capital
Tier 2 subordinated debt
General provisions and loss reserves

The Capital Conservation Buffer is meant to absorb losses in stress without breaching minimum requirements, so it must consist of the highest-quality capital, Common Equity Tier 1. Bonds and provisions do not qualify.
The Liquidity Coverage Ratio under Basel III requires banks to hold high-quality liquid assets sufficient to cover total net cash outflows over which period of stress?
7 days
90 days
30 days
One year

LCR measures short-term resilience: the stock of high-quality liquid assets should cover net cash outflows over a 30-day stress period. The one-year horizon relates to the Net Stable Funding Ratio instead.
Which of the following is an instrument of fiscal policy rather than monetary policy?
A reduction in the policy repo rate
An increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio
Open market sale of government securities
A cut in personal income tax rates

Fiscal policy is the government's use of taxation and public expenditure. Changing income tax rates is a fiscal measure, whereas repo rate, CRR and open market operations are monetary tools used by the RBI.
Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission?
Article 280
Article 112
Article 266
Article 148

Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission every five years or earlier, mainly to recommend the sharing of taxes between the Union and the States. Article 148 deals with the CAG.
The Union Budget is presented to Parliament as the 'Annual Financial Statement' under which Article of the Constitution?
Article 110
Article 112
Article 280
Article 265
Article 112 requires a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for each financial year, called the Annual Financial Statement. Article 110 defines a Money Bill.
The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), which insures bank deposits in India, is:
A department of the Ministry of Finance
A subsidiary of the State Bank of India
A wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India
A public sector general insurance company
DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI, set up under the DICGC Act, 1961. It insures deposits of eligible banks, including commercial banks and co-operative banks, up to a specified limit.
If the Indian rupee depreciates sharply against the US dollar, other things remaining equal, what is the most likely immediate effect?
Imported crude oil becomes cheaper in rupees
India's external debt falls in rupee terms
Foreign travel becomes cheaper for Indians
Indian exports become cheaper for buyers abroad

A weaker rupee means a foreign buyer needs fewer dollars to buy the same Indian goods, so exports become more competitive. Imports, foreign travel and dollar-denominated debt all become costlier in rupee terms.
In India's balance of payments, a Foreign Direct Investment inflow is recorded in which account?
Capital (financial) account
Current account
Merchandise trade account
Invisibles account

FDI creates ownership claims on assets, so it is recorded in the capital (financial) account. The current account covers trade in goods and services, primary income and transfers; invisibles are a part of it.
A Gini coefficient of zero for a country would indicate:
Perfect inequality, with one person earning all income
Perfect equality of income distribution
Zero growth in national income
An equal number of rich and poor households
The Gini coefficient ranges from 0 to 1 (or 0 to 100). A value of 0 means everyone has the same income, while a value of 1 means a single person receives all the income.
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of which committee?
Narasimham Committee
M. Narasimham Working Group on Lead Banks
B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD)
Raghuram Rajan Committee
NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 based on the recommendations of CRAFICARD, chaired by B. Sivaraman. The Narasimham Committees dealt with financial and banking sector reforms in the 1990s.

English Language.overview: The English Language section checks reading comprehension, grammar and vocabulary under time pressure. Passages are usually on economics, banking, policy or social issues, followed by questions on the main idea, inference, tone and the meaning of words in context. Grammar appears through error spotting, sentence improvement and fill-in-the-blanks, testing subject-verb agreement, tenses, prepositions, conditionals and comparatives. Vocabulary items cover synonyms, antonyms, idioms and one-word substitutions. Revise core grammar rules, read editorials daily, and practise eliminating options quickly.
questions:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Digital lending has widened access to credit for borrowers who were once ignored by formal lenders. A salaried worker in a small town can now obtain a small loan within minutes, using data from her phone instead of a long credit history. Yet speed has a cost. Some apps have concealed fees, harassed borrowers over delays and shared personal data without consent. Regulators have therefore insisted that loans be disbursed directly into the borrower's bank account and that the true annual cost be disclosed upfront. The aim is not to slow innovation but to make sure convenience does not come at the price of fairness.
Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
Digital lending apps should be banned because some of them harass borrowers
Regulators want to slow down innovation in lending to protect banks
