Small-town borrowers prefer lenders who rely on long credit histories
Digital lending widens access to credit but needs rules to keep it fair

The passage praises wider access, lists abuses, and says rules aim to keep convenience fair without slowing innovation. It never calls for a ban, and it explicitly denies that regulators want to slow innovation.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Digital lending has widened access to credit for borrowers who were once ignored by formal lenders. A salaried worker in a small town can now obtain a small loan within minutes, using data from her phone instead of a long credit history. Yet speed has a cost. Some apps have concealed fees, harassed borrowers over delays and shared personal data without consent. Regulators have therefore insisted that loans be disbursed directly into the borrower's bank account and that the true annual cost be disclosed upfront. The aim is not to slow innovation but to make sure convenience does not come at the price of fairness.
Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a problem with some lending apps?
Charging interest above a legal ceiling
Concealing fees from borrowers
Harassing borrowers over delays
Sharing personal data without consent
The passage lists concealed fees, harassment over delays and sharing data without consent. It mentions disclosure of the true annual cost but says nothing about any legal ceiling on interest rates.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Banks once treated climate change as a distant concern for environmental groups. That view is changing. A loan to a coastal factory may turn sour if rising seas flood its premises, and a coal plant may lose value long before its machinery wears out if cleaner energy becomes cheaper. Such risks are hard to price because they unfold over decades, while most loans are judged over a few years. Supervisors now ask banks to test how their portfolios would fare under different climate scenarios.
As used in the passage, the word 'sour' most nearly means:
taste unpleasantly acidic
become difficult to recover
grow larger in size
be signed again on new terms
In the passage a loan 'turns sour' when floods damage the borrower's premises, so the loan is unlikely to be repaid. The literal sense of an acidic taste does not fit a loan.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Each of the branch managers (A) / who attended the review meeting (B) / have been asked (C) / to submit a revised plan. (D)
The subject is 'Each', which is singular, so the verb must be 'has been asked'. The plural noun 'managers' inside the phrase 'of the branch managers' does not change the number of the subject.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither the chairman nor the directors (A) / was present at the meeting (B) / when the auditors (C) / presented their findings. (D)
With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Here the nearer subject is the plural 'directors', so 'was present' should be 'were present'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The new manager, along with his team, (A) / has been working hard (B) / to clear the backlog (C) / since the last two months. (D)
'Since' is used with a point of time, while 'for' is used with a period of time. 'Two months' is a period, so the phrase should read 'for the last two months'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The regional head insisted for (A) / an immediate review (B) / of all the pending (C) / loan applications. (D)
The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on', not 'for'. The correct phrase is 'insisted on an immediate review'. The remaining parts are grammatically correct.

Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The central bank's decision to leave rates unchanged was widely ________ by economists, most of whom had predicted a pause.
deterred
exempted
anticipated
retracted
The economists had predicted a pause, so the decision was expected, that is, 'anticipated'. 'Deterred', 'exempted' and 'retracted' do not make sense with a decision that economists had forecast.

Choose the pair of words that best fills the blanks.
Ever since the company ________ its distribution network, its rural sales ________ steadily.
has expanded / grew
expands / had grown
had expanded / will grow
expanded / have grown
'Ever since' with a past event (simple past 'expanded') is followed by the present perfect for a continuing result, 'have grown'. The other pairs mix tenses that do not fit this structure.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
IF I WOULD HAVE KNOWN about the deadline, I would have applied much earlier.
If I had known
If I have known
Had I would know
No improvement required
In a third conditional about an unreal past, the if-clause takes the past perfect: 'If I had known'. 'Would have' should never appear in the if-clause itself.

Choose the option that best replaces the part in capitals. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement required'.
Although she joined later, she is SENIOR THAN ME in the officers' cadre because of her rank.
more senior than me
senior to me
seniorer to me
No improvement required
Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than'. So the correct phrase is 'senior to me'; 'more senior than' is an unnecessary double form here.
Which of the following words is closest in meaning to PRUDENT, as in a prudent lender?
Reckless
Generous
Judicious
Hesitant
Prudent means acting with care and good judgement, especially about the future, which matches 'judicious'. 'Reckless' is its opposite, and 'hesitant' implies indecision rather than sound judgement.
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to AUSTERITY.
Severity
Thrift
Discipline
Extravagance
Austerity means strict economy and the avoidance of luxury. Its opposite is extravagance, meaning lavish spending. 'Thrift' and 'discipline' are close in meaning to austerity, not opposite.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To take something with a pinch of salt'.
To regard it with some doubt
To accept it eagerly and fully
To add a little extra detail to it
To deal with it very harshly
Taking something with a pinch of salt means not believing it completely and treating it with scepticism. It has nothing to do with eager acceptance or harsh treatment.
Choose the one word for: 'A system of government in which the wealthy class rules'.
Oligarchy
Plutocracy
Autocracy
Bureaucracy
Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy. Oligarchy, the tempting option, means rule by a small group, which need not be defined by wealth. Autocracy is rule by one person.

Quantitative Aptitude.overview: Quantitative Aptitude in RBI Grade B Phase I mixes speed-based calculation with problem solving. Common question types are simplification and approximation, number series (missing and wrong term), quadratic equations comparing x and y, and data interpretation from tables or charts. Arithmetic word problems cover simple and compound interest, profit and discount, partnership, time and work, pipes and cisterns, boats and streams, trains, ages, averages and probability. Learn shortcuts such as the two-year CI − SI formula, practise mental calculation, and attempt DI sets carefully since several questions share one table.
questions:
What will come in place of the question mark (?)
25% of 640 + 3/4 of 288 − 12² = ?
25% of 640 = 160 and 3/4 of 288 = 216. So the value is 160 + 216 − 144 = 232. Doing percentage and fraction parts first avoids errors.

What will come in place of the question mark (?)
7, 8, 12, 21, 37, ?
The differences are 1, 4, 9 and 16, which are the squares 1², 2², 3² and 4². The next difference is 5² = 25, so the answer is 37 + 25 = 62.

Find the wrong number in the series.
4, 6, 12, 32, 90, 315, 1260
Each term is multiplied by 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5 and 4 in turn: 4, 6, 12, 30, 90, 315, 1260. The fourth term should be 12 × 2.5 = 30, so 32 is wrong.

Two equations I and II are given. Solve both and choose the correct relationship between x and y.
I. x² − 11x + 30 = 0
II. y² − 13y + 42 = 0
x > y
x ≥ y
x < y
x ≤ y
I factorises as (x − 5)(x − 6) = 0, so x = 5 or 6. II gives (y − 6)(y − 7) = 0, so y = 6 or 7. Since x = 6 = y is possible, the relation is x ≤ y.
The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 8% per annum is ₹128. What is the sum?
For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (r/100)². So 128 = P × 0.0064, giving P = ₹20,000. This shortcut works only for two-year periods with annual compounding.
A trader marks an item 40% above its cost price and then allows two successive discounts of 10% and 5%. What is his profit percentage?
Taking cost as 100, the marked price is 140. After 10% off it is 126, and after a further 5% off it is 119.7. Profit is therefore 19.7%, not simply 40 − 15 = 25%.
A starts a business with ₹40,000. Five months later B joins with ₹60,000. At the end of the year the total profit is ₹45,000. What is B's share?

Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, in how many hours will it be full?
10 hours
8 hours
12 hours
9 hours
Net filling per hour = 1/12 + 1/15 − 1/20 = (5 + 4 − 3)/60 = 1/10. So the tank fills in 10 hours. Forgetting to subtract the outlet gives a much shorter time.
A boat covers 48 km downstream in 3 hours and 32 km upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
12 km/h
4 km/h
6 km/h
8 km/h
Downstream speed = 16 km/h and upstream speed = 8 km/h. Stream speed is half the difference, (16 − 8)/2 = 4 km/h. The 12 km/h figure is the boat's speed in still water.
A train 240 m long crosses a platform 360 m long in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
64 km/h
80 km/h
72 km/h
54 km/h
The train must cover its own length plus the platform: 600 m in 30 s, which is 20 m/s. Converting, 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.
The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 6 years, the ratio will be 7 : 9. What is A's present age?
18 years
21 years
12 years
15 years
Let the ages be 5k and 7k. Then (5k + 6)/(7k + 6) = 7/9, so 45k + 54 = 49k + 42, giving k = 3. A's present age is 5 × 3 = 15 years.
The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six results is 49 and that of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?
The sixth result is counted in both groups. Sixth = (6 × 49) + (6 × 52) − (11 × 50) = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56.
Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is a prime number?
Prime sums are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11, occurring in 1, 2, 4, 6 and 2 ways respectively, a total of 15 out of 36 outcomes. So the probability is 15/36 = 5/12.

The table shows loans disbursed (₹ crore) by a bank.
Year 2021: Housing 400, Education 100
Year 2022: Housing 450, Education 130
Year 2023: Housing 530, Education 130
By what percentage did the bank's total loans (housing + education) increase from 2021 to 2023?
Total loans were 400 + 100 = 500 in 2021 and 530 + 130 = 660 in 2023. The increase is 160, which is 160/500 × 100 = 32%.

The table shows loans disbursed (₹ crore) by a bank.
Year 2021: Housing 400, Education 100
Year 2022: Housing 450, Education 130
Year 2023: Housing 530, Education 130
What is the average annual housing loan disbursement over the three years?
₹450 crore
₹475 crore
₹445 crore
₹460 crore
Housing loans total 400 + 450 + 530 = 1,380 crore over three years. The average is 1,380 ÷ 3 = ₹460 crore.

Reasoning.overview: Reasoning in RBI Grade B Phase I is the most time-intensive section, dominated by puzzles and seating arrangements in linear, circular and floor-based formats. Alongside these, expect syllogisms, inequalities, blood relations, direction sense, coding-decoding, ranking and order, alphanumeric series and occasional clock or word-based questions. Practise drawing quick diagrams, fix definite placements first, then test the remaining cases. For syllogisms use Venn diagrams and accept a conclusion only if it is true in every possible case. Speed comes from regular timed practice of mixed sets.
questions:
Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V sit in a straight row facing north.
• S sits third from the left end.
• Only two persons sit between S and V.
• T sits immediately to the right of V.
• Q sits at one of the extreme ends.
• R is an immediate neighbour of S.
• U sits somewhere to the left of R.
Who sits exactly in the middle of the row?
R
P
S
U
S is third from left, so V is sixth and T seventh; Q must take the left end. R neighbours S at fourth, U fills second, P fifth: Q U S R P V T. The middle (fourth) seat is R's.

Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V sit in a straight row facing north.
• S sits third from the left end.
• Only two persons sit between S and V.
• T sits immediately to the right of V.
• Q sits at one of the extreme ends.
• R is an immediate neighbour of S.
• U sits somewhere to the left of R.
How many persons sit between U and V?
Two
Three
Four
One
The final order from left is Q, U, S, R, P, V, T. U is second and V is sixth, so S, R and P, three persons, sit between them.

Statements: All banks are lenders. Some lenders are brokers. No broker is an insurer.
Conclusions:
I. Some banks are brokers.
II. Some lenders are not insurers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Either I or II follows
Both I and II follow
The lenders that are brokers can never be insurers, so some lenders are not insurers, and II follows. Banks need not overlap with brokers at all, so I does not follow.

Statements: Some coins are notes. All notes are cheques. Some cheques are drafts.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are cheques.
II. Some drafts are coins.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Either I or II follows
Neither I nor II follows
Coins that are notes are also cheques, so some coins are cheques and I follows. Drafts are linked only to some cheques, which may not be the coin-notes, so II is not certain.

Statements: P > Q ≥ R = S, S < T ≤ U
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. U > R
Which conclusion(s) are definitely true?
Only I is true
Only II is true
Either I or II is true
Both I and II are true
From P > Q ≥ R = S we get P > S, so I is true. From U ≥ T > S = R we get U > R, so II is also true. Both conclusions hold.
M is the sister of N. N is the son of P. P is the husband of Q. R is the mother of P. How is M related to R?
Daughter
Niece
Granddaughter
Daughter-in-law
N is P's son and M is N's sister, so M is P's daughter. R is P's mother, which makes M the daughter of R's son, that is, R's granddaughter.
Riya walks 12 m towards the south, turns right and walks 5 m, then turns right again and walks 24 m. How far and in which direction is she now from her starting point?
13 m North-East
17 m North-West
12 m South-West
13 m North-West
Facing south, a right turn is west and the next right is north. She ends 5 m west and 24 − 12 = 12 m north of the start. Distance = √(25 + 144) = 13 m, towards the North-West.
In a certain code, CREDIT is written as XIVWRG. How is DEPOSIT written in that code?
WVKLHRG
WVKLHGR
WVLKHRG
XVKLHRG
Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X and so on). Applying this, D→W, E→V, P→K, O→L, S→H, I→R, T→G gives WVKLHRG.
If in a certain code CAT = 24 and DOG = 26, what is the code for BANK?
Each word's code is the sum of the alphabetical positions of its letters: C(3) + A(1) + T(20) = 24 and D(4) + O(15) + G(7) = 26. BANK = 2 + 1 + 14 + 11 = 28.
In a class of 45 students, Rohit ranks 14th from the top. Sunil is nine ranks below Rohit. What is Sunil's rank from the bottom?
22nd
24th
23rd
21st
Sunil is 14 + 9 = 23rd from the top. His rank from the bottom is 45 − 23 + 1 = 23rd. Forgetting to add 1 gives the tempting wrong answer 22nd.

Study the arrangement:
R 4 M # 7 K 2 @ T 9 P % 3 B & 6 H
How many symbols in the arrangement are immediately followed by a number?
Two
Four
One
Three
The symbols are #, @, % and &. # is followed by 7, % by 3 and & by 6, while @ is followed by the letter T. So three symbols qualify.

Five friends A, B, C, D and E have different heights.
• B is taller than C but shorter than A.
• E is shorter than only one person.
• D is taller than C.
• A is not the tallest.
Who is the tallest?
D
E
A
B
E is second tallest and A is not tallest, so the tallest is D (B and C are shorter than A). Then A is third, B fourth and C shortest: D > E > A > B > C.

Five friends A, B, C, D and E have different heights.
• B is taller than C but shorter than A.
• E is shorter than only one person.
• D is taller than C.
• A is not the tallest.
Who is the third tallest?
B
A
E
C
The clues give the order D > E > A > B > C. E is second, as it is shorter than only one person, so A is third tallest.
How many pairs of letters are there in the word PRODUCE, each of which has as many letters between them in the word as in the English alphabet (in either direction)?
Two
Three
One
None
Only R–U qualifies: two letters (O, D) lie between them in the word and two (S, T) in the alphabet. Pairs such as D–C or D–E are alphabet neighbours but not word neighbours, so they fail.
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40?
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30 × 3 − 5.5 × 40| = |90 − 220| = 130°. The minute hand moves 6° per minute and the hour hand 0.5° per minute.

General Intelligence & Reasoning.overview: This section tests verbal and non-verbal reasoning: analogies, classification (odd one out), number and letter series, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions, syllogisms, ranking, calendars, clocks, mathematical operations, seating arrangement and inequalities, along with figure-based items such as mirror images and paper folding. Most questions are short and rule-based, so speed comes from recognising common patterns: squares and cubes, alphabet positions, odd-day counting and the clock-angle formula. When revising, practise drawing quick diagrams for directions and family trees, use Venn diagrams for syllogisms, and always verify a found rule against every given pair before choosing an option.
questions:
Select the number that completes the analogy.
11 : 120 :: 13 : ?
Each first term is squared and then 1 is subtracted: 11² − 1 = 120. Applying the same rule, 13² − 1 = 169 − 1 = 168. The option 169 forgets the subtraction step.

Select the number that does NOT belong to the group.
27, 64, 100, 125
27, 64 and 125 are perfect cubes (3³, 4³ and 5³). 100 is a perfect square (10²) but not a perfect cube, so it is the odd one out.

Find the next term of the series.
2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
The terms are 1×2, 2×3, 3×4, 4×5 and 5×6, so the next term is 6×7 = 42. Equivalently the differences 4, 6, 8, 10 increase by 2, giving 30 + 12.

Find the next pair in the series.
AZ, BY, CX, ?
DW
EW
DV
DX
The first letters move forward one step (A, B, C, D) while the second letters move backward one step (Z, Y, X, W). Hence the next pair is DW.
In a certain code language, CHAIR is written as AFYGP. How will SOFA be written in that language?
RMDY
UQHC
QMDY
QMDZ
Every letter is moved two places back in the alphabet: C→A, H→F, A→Y, I→G, R→P. So S→Q, O→M, F→D and A→Y, giving QMDY. UQHC wrongly shifts letters forward.
If ROSE is coded as 6821, CHAIR as 73456 and PREACH as 961473, what is the code for SEARCH?
From the three codes: S = 2, E = 1, A = 4, R = 6, C = 7 and H = 3. Writing them in the order S-E-A-R-C-H gives 214673.
If 'A + B' means A is the mother of B and 'A × B' means A is the brother of B, then what does 'P × Q + R' mean about P with respect to R?
P is the father of R
P is the paternal uncle of R
P is the maternal uncle of R
P is the brother of R
P × Q means P is Q's brother, and Q + R means Q is R's mother. The brother of one's mother is one's maternal uncle, so P is R's maternal uncle.
A person is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise, then 135° anticlockwise, and then 180° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
South-East
North-East
North-West
South-West
Measuring clockwise from North: 0° + 90° = 90° (East), 90° − 135° = −45° (North-West), then −45° + 180° = 135°, which is South-East. North-West is the position before the last turn.

Statements:
Some pens are books.
No book is a bag.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are not bags.
II. Some bags are pens.
Only conclusion I follows
Neither I nor II follows
Both I and II follow
Only conclusion II follows
The pens that are books cannot be bags because no book is a bag, so 'some pens are not bags' is definite. Nothing tells us whether any bag is a pen, so II is only a possibility.
In a class, Neha is 12th from the top and 28th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
Total = (rank from top) + (rank from bottom) − 1 = 12 + 28 − 1 = 39. Adding without subtracting 1 counts Neha twice and gives the wrong answer 40.
On which day of the week did 15 August 1947 fall?
Friday
Sunday
Saturday
Thursday
1600 years give 0 odd days, 300 years give 1 and 46 years give 4, so 1946 years give 5. 1 January–15 August 1947 has 227 days = 3 odd days. Total 8 ≡ 1 odd day, so the date fell on a Friday.
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:20?
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30 × 4 − 5.5 × 20| = |120 − 110| = 10°. The hour hand moves 10° beyond the 4 in 20 minutes, which is why the hands do not overlap.
If 3 # 4 = 25 and 5 # 12 = 169, then what is 6 # 8?
The rule is a # b = a² + b²: 9 + 16 = 25 and 25 + 144 = 169. So 6 # 8 = 36 + 64 = 100. The option 196 is (6 + 8)², a common slip.

Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing North. C sits exactly in the middle and A sits to the immediate right of C. B sits at one of the extreme ends, and D does not sit next to C. Who sits to the immediate left of C?
B
E
D
A
C is 3rd and A is 4th from the left. B and D must take the two ends (D cannot be 2nd, as that is next to C), so the only seat left beside C, the 2nd one, goes to E.

Statement: P > Q ≥ R = S < T
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. Q > T
Only conclusion II follows
Neither I nor II follows
Both I and II follow
Only conclusion I follows
P > Q ≥ R = S gives P > S, so I is true. Q and T are both linked to S in opposite directions (Q ≥ S < T), so no definite relation exists between Q and T; II does not follow.

General Awareness.overview: General Awareness covers static general knowledge and science. Key areas are Indian polity (Constitution, Fundamental Rights and Duties, Parliament, amendments), modern, medieval and ancient Indian history, Indian and world geography (rivers, passes, soils, peaks), basic economics (budget and deficit concepts, banking terms), and everyday physics, chemistry and biology. Culture, awards and sports also appear. Focus on stable facts that can be learnt once: important Articles and Schedules, landmark events with dates, physical geography, and the reasoning behind science facts. Revise with short lists and comparison tables so that similar-looking options can be told apart quickly.
questions: The idea of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which country?
United States of America
Ireland
Canada
Erstwhile USSR
Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were inspired by the constitution of the former USSR and added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. Ireland, by contrast, inspired the Directive Principles of State Policy.
The Right to Education for children aged 6 to 14 years (Article 21A) was inserted into the Constitution by which amendment?
73rd Amendment Act, 1992
86th Amendment Act, 2002
42nd Amendment Act, 1976
44th Amendment Act, 1978
The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6–14. It also added a related Fundamental Duty for parents and guardians.
Which Schedule of the Constitution of India lists the officially recognised languages?
Ninth Schedule
Tenth Schedule
Seventh Schedule
Eighth Schedule
The Eighth Schedule lists the languages recognised by the Constitution. The Seventh Schedule contains the Union, State and Concurrent Lists, and the Tenth deals with anti-defection.
What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Rajya Sabha?
25 years
21 years
30 years
35 years
Article 84 sets the minimum age at 30 years for the Rajya Sabha and 25 years for the Lok Sabha. 35 years is the minimum age for the President and Vice-President.
Who is credited with founding the Indian National Congress in 1885?
Dadabhai Naoroji
W. C. Bonnerjee
Surendranath Banerjee
A. O. Hume

Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, took the initiative to found the Congress in 1885. W. C. Bonnerjee presided over its first session in Bombay, which makes him a tempting wrong choice.
The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by which Governor-General?
Warren Hastings
Lord Dalhousie
Lord Cornwallis
Lord Wellesley
Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793, fixing revenue permanently with zamindars. Wellesley is linked to the Subsidiary Alliance and Dalhousie to the Doctrine of Lapse.
The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was built by which Mughal ruler?
Shah Jahan
Humayun
Aurangzeb
Akbar
Akbar built the Buland Darwaza around 1575–76 to commemorate his Gujarat campaign. Fatehpur Sikri itself was Akbar's capital; Shah Jahan is associated with the Taj Mahal and Red Fort.
Which mountain pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
Zoji La
Nathu La
Bomdi La
Shipki La
Zoji La links the Kashmir valley with Ladakh on the Srinagar–Leh route. Nathu La is in Sikkim, Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh and Bomdi La in Arunachal Pradesh.
Black soil (regur) of the Deccan plateau is best suited for growing which crop?
Tea
Rubber
Cotton
Jute
Black soil retains moisture well and is rich in lime and magnesium, making it ideal for cotton, hence the name 'black cotton soil'. Tea needs acidic hill soils and jute grows in alluvial delta soils.
Which is the highest peak in South India?
Dhupgarh
Mahendragiri
Anamudi
Doddabetta
Anamudi (about 2,695 m) in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala is the highest peak south of the Himalayas. Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Nilgiris, and Dhupgarh is in the Satpura range.
Fiscal deficit of the government is best defined as:
Fiscal deficit minus interest payments on past debt
Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts
Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
Total expenditure minus revenue receipts and all borrowings

Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), i.e. it equals the government's borrowing requirement. Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts is the revenue deficit; deficit minus interest is primary deficit.
Which group of chemicals is chiefly responsible for depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer?
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
Nitrogen and argon
Carbon dioxide and methane
Sulphur dioxide and ammonia
CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that break down ozone molecules. Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases linked to global warming, not the main cause of ozone depletion.
Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
Cylindrical mirror
Convex mirror
Concave mirror
Plane mirror
A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and gives a wider field of view, which helps drivers see more traffic behind. Concave mirrors are used in torches and shaving mirrors.
The hormone insulin is secreted by which organ of the human body?
Adrenal gland
Pancreas
Thyroid gland
Liver
Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas and lowers blood glucose. The liver stores glucose as glycogen but does not secrete insulin.
Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
Chlorine
Fluorine
Nitrogen
Oxygen

Fluorine, with a value of about 4.0, is the most electronegative element. Oxygen (about 3.4) is second; chlorine has a higher electron affinity than fluorine but lower electronegativity, which often confuses students.

Quantitative Aptitude.overview: Quantitative Aptitude covers arithmetic (number system, HCF-LCM, percentages, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, ratio, averages, mixtures, time and work, pipes, speed-distance-time, boats), algebra (identities), geometry, mensuration, trigonometry and data interpretation. Questions reward knowing shortcut formulas such as the 2xy/(x+y) average-speed rule, unit-digit cycles and (a + b)² identities, and avoiding traps such as changing bases in percentage questions. Revise standard trigonometric values, area and volume formulas, and practise calculating percentages from small tables quickly, since accuracy matters with negative marking.
questions: What is the unit digit of 7⁹⁵?
Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Since 95 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 4, the unit digit equals that of 7³, which is 3.
What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?
12 = 2²×3, 18 = 2×3² and 30 = 2×3×5. Taking the highest power of each prime: 2² × 3² × 5 = 180. 360 is a common multiple but not the least one.
A's salary is 25% more than B's salary. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's?
If B = 100, then A = 125. B is less than A by 25, and 25/125 × 100 = 20%. The base changes to A's salary, which is why the answer is not 25%.
A trader sells two articles for ₹1,200 each. He gains 20% on one and loses 20% on the other. What is his overall result?
Loss of 4%
No profit, no loss
Loss of 2%
Gain of 4%
Cost prices are 1200/1.2 = ₹1,000 and 1200/0.8 = ₹1,500, total ₹2,500. Total selling price is ₹2,400, so loss = 100/2500 × 100 = 4%. Equal gain and loss percentages on equal SP always give a loss.
A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
Doubling means interest equals the principal, i.e. 100% in 8 years. Rate = 100/8 = 12.5% per annum, using SI = P × R × T/100 with SI = P.
What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 for 3 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually?
Amount = 8000 × (1.1)³ = 8000 × 1.331 = ₹10,648. CI = 10,648 − 8,000 = ₹2,648. ₹2,400 is the simple interest for the same period.
₹7,800 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. What is B's share?
Multiplying by the LCM 12, the ratio becomes 6 : 4 : 3, totalling 13 parts. One part = 7800/13 = ₹600, so B gets 4 × 600 = ₹2,400. ₹3,600 is A's share.
The average of five numbers is 24. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers becomes 21. What is the number removed?
Sum of five numbers = 5 × 24 = 120; sum of remaining four = 4 × 21 = 84. The removed number = 120 − 84 = 36.
Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If both are opened together in an empty tank, in how many hours will it be filled?
25 hours
12 hours
6 hours
30 hours
Net filling per hour = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30 of the tank, so it fills in 30 hours. 6 hours would be the answer only if both pipes were filling.
A man goes from his house to the office at 40 km/h and returns along the same route at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
48 km/h
45 km/h
52 km/h
50 km/h
For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h. The simple average 50 km/h is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed.
A boat goes 18 km/h downstream and 12 km/h upstream. What is the speed of the stream?
15 km/h
5 km/h
6 km/h
3 km/h
Stream speed = (downstream − upstream)/2 = (18 − 12)/2 = 3 km/h. The value 15 km/h is the speed of the boat in still water.
If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, what is the value of a² + b²?
a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab = 100 − 42 = 58. Check: a = 7 and b = 3 satisfy both conditions, and 49 + 9 = 58.
What is the value of sin²30° + cos²60° + tan²45°?
sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2, so each square is 1/4, and tan 45° = 1. The sum is 1/4 + 1/4 + 1 = 3/2.
The circumference of a circle is 88 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7)
1232 cm²
154 cm²
308 cm²
616 cm²
2πr = 88 gives r = 88 × 7/44 = 14 cm. Area = πr² = 22/7 × 14 × 14 = 616 cm². 154 cm² is the area for radius 7 cm.
Monthly output of a factory (units): January 400, February 500, March 450, April 650. By what percentage did April's output exceed the average output of January to March?
Average for January–March = (400 + 500 + 450)/3 = 450 units. April exceeded it by 200, and 200/450 × 100 = 44 4/9% (about 44.4%).

English Comprehension.overview: English Comprehension checks vocabulary, grammar and reading skills. Vocabulary items include synonyms, antonyms, idioms and phrases, one-word substitutions and spelling. Grammar items include error spotting, fill-in-the-blanks, sentence improvement, active-passive voice and direct-indirect speech, testing rules such as subject-verb agreement, fixed prepositions and correlative conjunctions. Reading comprehension and cloze passages test understanding of the main idea and word meanings in context. Revise grammar rules with examples, learn commonly confused words, and read short editorials regularly to build speed and contextual understanding.
questions:
Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The minister gave a CANDID reply when reporters asked about the delay.
Cautious
Rigid
Frank
Secretive
'Candid' means honest and straightforward in speech, which matches 'frank'. 'Secretive' is nearly its opposite, while 'cautious' and 'rigid' describe unrelated qualities.

Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.
My grandfather led a FRUGAL life even after he became rich.
Thrifty
Extravagant
Careful
Modest
'Frugal' means careful and sparing with money. Its opposite is 'extravagant', meaning spending too much. 'Thrifty' and 'careful' are synonyms, not antonyms.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil'.
To work or study late into the night
To waste money on useless things
To lose one's temper suddenly
To destroy evidence of a mistake
'To burn the midnight oil' refers to staying up late to work or study, originally by the light of an oil lamp. It has nothing to do with waste or anger.
Select the one word for: 'A person who is unable to pay his or her debts'.
Indolent
Inveterate
Insolent
Insolvent
'Insolvent' describes a person or firm unable to pay debts. 'Insolent' means rude, 'indolent' means lazy and 'inveterate' means habitual; they look similar but differ in meaning.
Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
Embarass
Embarrass
Emberrass
Embarras
The correct spelling is 'embarrass', with double 'r' and double 's'. The other options drop one of the doubled letters or change the vowel.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Neither the manager nor his assistants / was present / at the meeting / held yesterday.
Neither the manager nor his assistants
held yesterday
at the meeting
was present
With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Here the nearer subject 'assistants' is plural, so 'was present' should be 'were present'.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
He is senior than me / in the office / by three years / and earns more.
and earns more
in the office
He is senior than me
by three years
Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than'. The correct form is 'He is senior to me'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
The thief was caught ______ the act of breaking the lock.
on
by
in
at
The fixed expression is 'caught in the act', meaning caught while doing something wrong. The other prepositions do not form this idiom.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
Hardly had I reached the station ______ the train left.
when
then
but
than
'Hardly' and 'scarcely' are followed by 'when' (or 'before'). 'Than' is used with 'no sooner', which is the usual source of confusion.

Select the most appropriate improvement for the underlined part.
The number of students in the class 'are increasing' every year.
is increasing
were increasing
are increased
have been increasing
The subject is 'the number', which is singular, so the verb must be singular: 'is increasing'. 'A number of students' would take a plural verb, but 'the number of' does not.
Select the correct passive form of: Who wrote this letter?
By whom has this letter been written?
Who was written this letter by?
By whom this letter was written?
By whom was this letter written?
An interrogative with 'who' becomes 'by whom' in the passive, keeping question word order: By whom + was + object + past participle. The present perfect option changes the tense.
Select the correct indirect form of: She said to me, "Please help me."
She told to me that please help her.
She requested me to help her.
She requested me that I help me.
She said me to please help her.
A polite request with 'please' is reported with 'requested', and the imperative becomes a to-infinitive. The pronoun 'me' changes to 'her' to refer back to the speaker.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Rainwater harvesting is an old practice that has found new relevance in Indian cities. As groundwater levels fall, many housing societies now collect rooftop runoff and channel it into recharge pits instead of letting it flow into drains. The method is inexpensive and needs little maintenance, yet its benefits depend on cleaning the filters regularly before every monsoon.
According to the passage, what do the benefits of rainwater harvesting depend on?
The number of drains available in the city
Regular cleaning of filters before the monsoon
The total cost of building large recharge pits
Housing societies recruiting full-time staff

The last sentence says the benefits 'depend on cleaning the filters regularly before every monsoon'. The passage calls the method inexpensive and low-maintenance, so cost and staffing are not the limiting factors.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Rainwater harvesting is an old practice that has found new relevance in Indian cities. As groundwater levels fall, many housing societies now collect rooftop runoff and channel it into recharge pits instead of letting it flow into drains. The method is inexpensive and needs little maintenance, yet its benefits depend on cleaning the filters regularly before every monsoon.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'relevance' as used in the passage?
Expense
Importance
Difficulty
Antiquity
The passage says an old practice has found new relevance because groundwater is falling, i.e. it has become important or applicable again. 'Antiquity' refers to oldness, the opposite idea.

Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals.
The fame of most viral videos is EPHEMERAL.
Permanent
Transient
Fleeting
Momentary
'Ephemeral' means lasting a very short time. 'Fleeting', 'transient' and 'momentary' are all synonyms, so the only antonym is 'permanent'.

General Intelligence.overview: This section tests logical and analytical reasoning through verbal and non-verbal questions: analogies, classification (odd one out), number and letter series, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions and distance, ranking, syllogisms, mathematical operations, calendars, clocks, mirror images and simple seating arrangements. Most questions follow a hidden pattern, so practise spotting rules quickly: alphabet positions, squares and cubes, and common series patterns. Draw quick diagrams for directions, family trees and arrangements, and use Venn diagrams for syllogisms. Speed and accuracy both matter because of negative marking.
questions:
Select the number that completes the analogy.
7 : 49 :: 12 : ?
The second number is the square of the first: 7 × 7 = 49. Applying the same rule, 12 × 12 = 144. The option 169 is the square of 13, not 12.

Select the letter-cluster that completes the analogy.
DOG : FQI :: CAT : ?
ECV
DBU
EDV
FCW
Each letter of DOG moves two places forward to give FQI (D→F, O→Q, G→I). Moving each letter of CAT two places forward gives C→E, A→C, T→V, so the answer is ECV.

Select the odd number out.
121, 169, 225, 290
121, 169 and 225 are perfect squares of 11, 13 and 15 respectively. 290 lies between 17² = 289 and 18² = 324, so it is not a perfect square and is the odd one out.

Find the next term of the series.
3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?
Each term is double the previous term plus 2: 3×2+2 = 8, 8×2+2 = 18, 18×2+2 = 38, 38×2+2 = 78. Hence the next term is 78×2+2 = 158.

Find the next letter in the series.
B, E, I, N, ?
S
T
U
R
Using alphabet positions, B=2, E=5, I=9, N=14. The gaps increase by one each time: +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6, giving 14+6 = 20, which is the letter T.
In a certain code language, MANGO is written as NBOHP. How will APPLE be written in that code language?
BQQME
BQQMF
ZOOKD
BPQMF
Every letter of MANGO is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet (M→N, A→B and so on). Applying the same +1 shift to APPLE gives A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F, that is BQQMF.
If CAB = 6 in a certain code (the sum of the alphabet positions of its letters), what is the value of FACE?
In CAB, C=3, A=1 and B=2, totalling 6. Using the same rule, FACE gives F=6, A=1, C=3 and E=5, and their sum is 6+1+3+5 = 15.
Pointing to a girl, Ravi said, "Her mother is the only daughter of my mother." How is the girl related to Ravi?
Niece
Daughter
Sister
Cousin
The only daughter of Ravi's mother is Ravi's sister. The girl's mother is therefore Ravi's sister, which makes the girl the daughter of his sister, that is, Ravi's niece.
Sunil walks 5 km towards the South, then turns left and walks 12 km. How far and in which direction is he now from his starting point?
13 km, South-West
17 km, South-East
13 km, South-East
7 km, North-East
Turning left while facing South means facing East. His position is 5 km South and 12 km East of the start, so the distance is √(5² + 12²) = 13 km and the direction is South-East.
In a row of 40 students, Meena is 14th from the left end. What is her position from the right end?
26th
28th
27th
25th
Position from the right = total − position from the left + 1 = 40 − 14 + 1 = 27. Forgetting to add 1 gives 26th, which is a common mistake.

Statements:
All pens are books.
Some books are bags.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are bags.
II. Some books are pens.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Since all pens are books, some books are definitely pens, so II follows. The books that are bags need not include any pens, so I is only a possibility and does not follow.

If '+' means '×', '−' means '+', '×' means '÷' and '÷' means '−', what is the value of:
8 + 3 − 12 × 4 ÷ 5
Replacing the signs gives 8 × 3 + 12 ÷ 4 − 5. Following BODMAS, this is 24 + 3 − 5 = 22.
If 1 January 2026 is a Thursday, which day of the week will 1 March 2026 be?
Saturday
Monday
Sunday
Friday
2026 is not a leap year, so January (31) and February (28) together have 59 days. 59 leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 7, so the day moves three ahead from Thursday to Sunday.
A wall clock shows the time 4:15. What time will its mirror image show?
For a mirror image, subtract the shown time from 11:60 (that is, 12:00). 11:60 − 4:15 = 7:45. Subtracting from 12:00 without borrowing correctly often leads to 8:45.

Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing North. R sits in the middle. P sits at the extreme left end. T sits immediately to the right of R. Q is not an immediate neighbour of P. Who sits second from the left end?
Q
T
R
S
P is 1st, R is 3rd and T is 4th. Q and S occupy places 2 and 5. Q cannot sit next to P, so Q is 5th and S is 2nd from the left.

General Awareness.overview: General Awareness covers static general knowledge and science: Indian polity and the Constitution, ancient, medieval and modern history, Indian and world geography, basic economics, and everyday physics, chemistry and biology. Questions are short and factual, so wide reading and regular revision matter more than depth. Focus on important Articles, Parliament procedures, key battles and reform movements, rivers and physical features, vitamins and diseases, and common chemical formulae. Make short revision notes and revisit them often, as this section can be attempted quickly and frees up time for others.
questions: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form?
Article 14
Article 21
Article 17
Article 19
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its practice an offence punishable by law. Article 14 deals with equality before law, while Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.
Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of the Indian Parliament?
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
President of India
Vice-President of India
Prime Minister of India

Under Article 108, the President summons a joint sitting, but it is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. In the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker presides, not the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Battle of Plassey, which helped the East India Company gain control over Bengal, was fought in which year?
The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah. The Battle of Buxar (1764) later strengthened Company rule, and 1761 is the Third Battle of Panipat.
Who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
Raja Ram Mohan Roy
Swami Dayanand Saraswati
Swami Vivekananda
Keshab Chandra Sen
Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 and gave the call 'Go back to the Vedas'. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj, and Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission.
Which river of peninsular India is popularly called 'Dakshin Ganga'?
Krishna
Godavari
Kaveri
Narmada
The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India and is therefore called Dakshin Ganga or the Ganga of the South. It rises at Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and drains into the Bay of Bengal.
The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
Tripura
Odisha
Rajasthan
Gujarat
The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies entirely to its south, so the line does not cross it.
Scurvy, marked by bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds, is caused by a deficiency of which vitamin?
Vitamin D
Vitamin A
Vitamin B1
Vitamin C

Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed to make collagen, so its deficiency causes scurvy. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and vitamin B1 deficiency causes beriberi.
What is the pH of pure water at 25°C?
Pure water at 25°C is neutral, with equal concentrations of hydrogen and hydroxide ions, giving a pH of 7. Values below 7 are acidic and values above 7 are basic.
The ancient Indian treatise 'Arthashastra' on statecraft and economics is attributed to:
Kalidasa
Banabhatta
Kautilya
Megasthenes
The Arthashastra is attributed to Kautilya, also known as Chanakya, adviser to Chandragupta Maurya. Megasthenes, a Greek envoy, wrote Indica, and Kalidasa was a poet and dramatist.
What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
Na₂CO₃
NaCl
NaHCO₃
CaCO₃
Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃. Na₂CO₃ is washing soda, NaCl is common salt and CaCO₃ is calcium carbonate, found in limestone and marble.
In which of the following media does sound travel the fastest?
Steel
Water
Air
Vacuum
Sound needs a medium and travels fastest in solids because their particles are tightly packed and elastic. It is slower in liquids, slower still in gases, and cannot travel through a vacuum at all.
Which body releases the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for rural, urban and combined India?
Reserve Bank of India
National Statistical Office
NITI Aayog
Finance Commission

The CPI (Rural, Urban and Combined) is compiled and released by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The RBI uses CPI inflation for its monetary policy but does not publish it.
The idea of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution was mainly borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
United Kingdom
United States of America
Ireland
Canada

Fundamental Rights are modelled mainly on the Bill of Rights in the US Constitution. Directive Principles came from Ireland, parliamentary government from the United Kingdom and a federation with a strong Centre from Canada.
The Battle of Talikota (1565) led to the decline of which empire?
Mughal Empire
Chola Empire
Maratha Empire
Vijayanagara Empire
In 1565 the combined Deccan Sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara army at Talikota, and the capital Hampi was sacked. The Marathas rose much later, and the Chola Empire had ended centuries earlier.
Who was the first and only Indian to serve as Governor-General of independent India?
Lord Mountbatten
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
C. Rajagopalachari

C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Lord Mountbatten in 1948 and served till the post was abolished in 1950. Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India but was not Indian; Rajendra Prasad became the first President.

Quantitative Aptitude.overview: Quantitative Aptitude covers arithmetic and elementary mathematics up to Class 10 level: number system, HCF and LCM, percentages, ratio and proportion, mixtures, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest, time and work, pipes, speed and trains, algebraic identities, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry and basic data interpretation. Learn standard shortcuts such as successive-percentage formulas, alligation and remainder cycles. Memorise squares, cubes and common fractions to speed up calculation, and always check units such as m/s versus km/h before choosing an answer.
questions: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 126?
84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 126 = 2 × 3² × 7. Taking the lowest power of each common prime gives 2 × 3 × 7 = 42. Both 21 and 14 are common factors, but not the highest.
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar remains the same?
Required reduction = rise ÷ (100 + rise) × 100 = 25 ÷ 125 × 100 = 20%. Reducing by 25% would actually lower the expenditure, because the base price is now higher.
Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equivalent to a single discount of:
After a 20% discount, ₹100 becomes ₹80, and a further 10% off gives ₹72. The total discount is ₹28 on ₹100, that is 28%, not the simple sum of 30%.
What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
Amount = 10,000 × (1.1)² = ₹12,100, so compound interest = ₹2,100. Simple interest would be ₹2,000; the extra ₹100 is interest earned on the first year's interest.
If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : B : C?
Make B common by taking the LCM of 3 and 4, which is 12. A : B = 8 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 15, so A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.
In what ratio must rice costing ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹55 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹45 per kg?
By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1. The mixture price is closer to ₹40, so more of the cheaper rice is needed.
A train 150 m long crosses a pole in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
15 km/h
45 km/h
60 km/h
54 km/h
To cross a pole the train covers its own length, so speed = 150 ÷ 10 = 15 m/s. Converting, 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h. The figure 15 is the speed in m/s, not km/h.
Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe B can fill it in 18 hours. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
7 hours 12 minutes
7 hours 30 minutes
6 hours
7 hours 20 minutes
Together they fill 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the tank per hour, so the time is 36/5 = 7.2 hours. 0.2 hour is 12 minutes, giving 7 hours 12 minutes.
If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
Squaring both sides gives x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23. Adding 2 instead of subtracting gives the tempting wrong answer 27.
What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
84 cm²
91 cm²
78 cm²
105 cm²
What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
440 cm³
1540 cm³
1440 cm³
3080 cm³
Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 7 × 7 × 10 = 1540 cm³. The value 440 cm³ is the curved surface area, which uses 2πrh instead.
If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is an acute angle, what is the value of sin θ + cos θ?
With opposite side 3 and adjacent side 4, the hypotenuse is 5. So sin θ = 3/5 and cos θ = 4/5, and their sum is 7/5.
A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
Take CP = ₹100. Marked price = ₹140, and after a 15% discount, SP = 140 × 0.85 = ₹119. Profit = ₹19 on ₹100, that is 19%. Simply subtracting 15 from 40 wrongly gives 25%.
What is the remainder when 2³¹ is divided by 7?
2³ = 8 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 7. Since 31 = 3 × 10 + 1, 2³¹ = (2³)¹⁰ × 2, which leaves remainder 1 × 2 = 2.
A company's sales (in ₹ lakh) were: 2021 – 120, 2022 – 150, 2023 – 135, 2024 – 180. What was the percentage increase in sales from 2023 to 2024?
Increase = 180 − 135 = 45 lakh. Percentage increase = 45 ÷ 135 × 100 = 33⅓%. Dividing by the new value 180 instead of the old value gives 25%, which is wrong.

English Language.overview: English Language tests vocabulary, grammar and comprehension. Expect synonyms, antonyms, idioms and phrases, one-word substitution and spelling, along with error spotting, fill-in-the-blanks, sentence improvement, active-passive voice, direct-indirect speech, sentence rearrangement and short comprehension passages. Revise subject-verb agreement, tenses, articles, prepositions and the subjunctive mood. Read regularly to build vocabulary in context, and for passages, answer only from what the text actually says rather than from your own general knowledge.
questions: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSOLETE, as in 'obsolete machinery'.
Obscure
Essential
Durable
Outdated
Obsolete means no longer in use or out of date, so 'outdated' is the closest synonym. 'Obscure' looks similar but means unclear or little known.
Choose the word opposite in meaning to FRUGAL, as in 'a frugal lifestyle'.
Extravagant
Thrifty
Modest
Careful
Frugal means careful and sparing with money. Its opposite is extravagant, meaning spending too much. 'Thrifty' and 'careful' are close to synonyms, not antonyms.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil'.
To waste money on useless things
To lose one's temper very quickly
To work or study late into the night
To start a quarrel without reason
'To burn the midnight oil' means to stay up late working or studying, from the old practice of reading by oil lamps at night. It has nothing to do with wasting money or anger.
Select the one word for: 'A speech delivered without any preparation'.
Monologue
Soliloquy
Extempore
Eulogy

An extempore speech is given on the spot without preparation. A soliloquy is speaking one's thoughts aloud alone, a eulogy praises someone (usually after death), and a monologue is a long speech by one person.
Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
Accomodate
Acommodate
Acomodate
Accommodate
The correct spelling is 'accommodate', with a double 'c' and a double 'm'. The other options drop one of these doubled letters, a very common spelling error.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
One of my friends / have gone / to Mumbai / for higher studies.
One of my friends
have gone
to Mumbai
for higher studies
The subject is 'one', which is singular, even though 'friends' is plural. The verb must agree with 'one', so 'have gone' should be 'has gone'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate article.
She is ______ honest woman.
a
the
no article
an
'Honest' begins with a silent 'h', so it starts with a vowel sound. The article 'an' is used before a vowel sound, giving 'an honest woman'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb form.
By the time we reached the station, the train ______.
has left
will leave
had left
leaves
When one past action happened before another past action, the earlier one takes the past perfect. The train left before we reached, so 'had left' is correct.

Select the most appropriate improvement for the underlined part.
'If I was you', I would accept the offer.
If I were you
If I am you
If I had been you
No improvement
Imaginary or unreal situations in the present use the subjunctive 'were' for all subjects. So the correct form is 'If I were you, I would accept the offer'.
Select the correct passive form of: The committee has approved the proposal.
The proposal has been approved by the committee.
The proposal was approved by the committee.
The proposal had been approved by the committee.
The proposal is being approved by the committee.
The active sentence is in the present perfect tense, so the passive uses 'has been' with the past participle: 'The proposal has been approved by the committee.' The other options change the tense.
Select the correct indirect form of: He said, "I am tired."
He said that I was tired.
He said that he is tired.
He says that he was tired.
He said that he was tired.
With a past reporting verb, the present 'am' changes to 'was' and the pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'. The reporting verb 'said' itself stays unchanged.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Rainwater harvesting is the practice of collecting and storing rain that falls on rooftops and open ground. In many Indian towns, the stored water is used to recharge wells and borewells, which reduces dependence on distant reservoirs. The method is cheap, but it works only when tanks and pipes are cleaned before the monsoon.
According to the passage, rainwater harvesting works only when:
the town is close to a large reservoir
wells and borewells are dug again every year
tanks and pipes are cleaned before the monsoon
rain falls only on rooftops and not on open ground

The last sentence states that the method works only when tanks and pipes are cleaned before the monsoon. The passage actually says harvesting reduces dependence on distant reservoirs, so proximity to one is not a condition.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Rainwater harvesting is the practice of collecting and storing rain that falls on rooftops and open ground. In many Indian towns, the stored water is used to recharge wells and borewells, which reduces dependence on distant reservoirs. The method is cheap, but it works only when tanks and pipes are cleaned before the monsoon.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'dependence' as used in the passage?
Freedom
Distance
Reliance
Shortage
In the passage, harvested water reduces dependence on distant reservoirs, that is, the need to rely on them. 'Reliance' carries this meaning, while 'freedom' is almost its opposite.

Arrange the sentences in a logical order.
P: she boarded the bus to the city.
Q: Early in the morning, Asha packed her bag.
R: After a long ride, she reached her aunt's house.
S: Then she walked to the bus stand.
QPSR
QSPR
SQPR
QSRP
Q introduces Asha and the time, so it comes first. She then walks to the bus stand (S), boards the bus (P) and finally reaches her aunt's house after the ride (R), giving QSPR.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
The ______ of the new policy will be felt mostly by small traders.
effect
affect
affection
effort
A noun meaning 'result' is needed after 'the', so 'effect' fits. 'Affect' is normally a verb meaning to influence, and 'effort' or 'affection' do not suit the sense of the sentence.

Numerical Ability.overview: Numerical Ability in SSC MTS tests school-level arithmetic: number system, divisibility, HCF/LCM, fractions and decimals, simplification (BODMAS), percentages, ratio and proportion, averages, profit, loss and discount, simple and compound interest, time and work, pipes and cisterns, time-speed-distance (including trains and boats) and basic mensuration of plane figures. Questions are short and calculation-based, so speed matters. While revising, memorise squares, cubes and percentage–fraction equivalents, practise unit conversions such as km/h to m/s, and learn the standard shortcuts for successive percentage change, work-rate and relative speed problems.
questions: What is the LCM of 18, 24 and 30?
18 = 2 × 3², 24 = 2³ × 3 and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. Taking the highest power of each prime gives 2³ × 3² × 5 = 360. 180 is not divisible by 24.
What is 12.5% of 640?
12.5% equals the fraction 1/8, so 12.5% of 640 = 640 ÷ 8 = 80. Remembering common fraction equivalents of percentages saves time in the exam.
A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
Take CP = ₹100. Marked price = ₹140. After a 15% discount, SP = 140 × 0.85 = ₹119. Profit = ₹19 on ₹100, i.e. 19%. Subtracting 15 from 40 to get 25% is the common trap.
What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
Amount = 8000 × (1.1)² = ₹9,680, so CI = 9,680 − 8,000 = ₹1,680. Simple interest would be only ₹1,600; the extra ₹80 is interest on the first year's interest.
A train 240 m long runs at 72 km/h. How long will it take to cross a platform 160 m long?
12 seconds
18 seconds
20 seconds
24 seconds
72 km/h = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. To cross a platform the train covers its own length plus the platform length: 240 + 160 = 400 m. Time = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 seconds.
The average of five numbers is 42. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 40. What is the number removed?
Sum of five numbers = 5 × 42 = 210. Sum of the remaining four = 4 × 40 = 160. The removed number = 210 − 160 = 50.
Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe B can fill it in 18 hours. If both are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
7 hours 30 minutes
6 hours
7 hours 12 minutes
15 hours
In one hour the pipes fill 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the tank. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 hours, which is 7 hours and 0.2 × 60 = 12 minutes.
Find the value of (0.25 × 0.4) ÷ 0.05.
0.25 × 0.4 = 0.1. Then 0.1 ÷ 0.05 = 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Shifting the decimal points equally in numerator and denominator avoids errors.
What is the area of a circle of radius 14 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
616 cm²
88 cm²
308 cm²
1232 cm²
Area = πr² = 22/7 × 14 × 14 = 616 cm². 88 cm is the circumference (2πr), a frequent mix-up between the two formulas.
15 men can complete a piece of work in 24 days. How many men are needed to complete the same work in 18 days?
Total work = 15 × 24 = 360 man-days. Men required for 18 days = 360 ÷ 18 = 20. More men are needed because fewer days are available (inverse proportion).
If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then what is A : B : C?
Make B common: multiply the first ratio by 4 (8 : 12) and the second by 3 (12 : 15). So A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar remains unchanged?
Reduction = 25/(100 + 25) × 100 = 20%. Check: 1.25 × 0.80 = 1, so spending stays the same. Reducing by 25% would actually cut expenditure.
What is the smallest number that must be added to 1000 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 23?
1000 ÷ 23 leaves remainder 11 (23 × 43 = 989). Adding 23 − 11 = 12 gives 1012 = 23 × 44. Choosing 11 confuses the remainder with the amount to be added.
A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How long will the boat take to go 36 km downstream and come back the same distance?
4.8 hours
5 hours
5.5 hours
4 hours
Downstream speed = 18 km/h, so 36 km takes 2 hours. Upstream speed = 12 km/h, so 36 km takes 3 hours. Total time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours.
A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
If the sum doubles, interest equals the principal. So P × R × 8 / 100 = P, giving R = 100/8 = 12.5% per annum.

Reasoning Ability.overview: Reasoning Ability covers verbal and non-verbal reasoning: analogies, classification (odd one out), number and letter series, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions and distance, ranking and order, calendar and clock problems, mathematical operations, syllogisms, inequalities, Venn diagrams and simple seating arrangements. Most questions can be solved in under a minute if you follow a method. Revise alphabet positions (A = 1 to Z = 26), draw quick diagrams for directions and family trees, apply odd-day rules for calendars and the 30H − 5.5M formula for clocks, and check every syllogism conclusion against all possible cases.
questions:
Select the word that completes the analogy.
Bird : Nest :: Bee : ?
Den
Burrow
Stable
Hive
A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive. A den is a lion's or fox's home, a burrow a rabbit's and a stable a horse's.

Select the number that does not belong to the group.
27, 64, 125, 150
27 = 3³, 64 = 4³ and 125 = 5³ are perfect cubes. 150 is not a perfect cube, so it is the odd one out.

Find the next term of the series.
3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
Each term is double the previous term plus 1: 3×2+1 = 7, 7×2+1 = 15, and so on. So 63 × 2 + 1 = 127.

Find the next letter of the series.
B, E, H, K, ?
M
O
N
L
The letters move forward three places each time: B(2), E(5), H(8), K(11). The next is position 14, which is N.
In a certain code language, FRIEND is written as HUMJTK. How will CANDLE be written in that language?
EDRJRL
ECRIRL
EDQIRL
EDRIRL
The letters are shifted forward by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 places in order (F→H, R→U, I→M …). Applying the same shifts to CANDLE gives E, D, R, I, R, L = EDRIRL.
If 2 ★ 3 = 13 and 4 ★ 1 = 17, then what is the value of 5 ★ 2?
The rule is a ★ b = a² + b²: 4 + 9 = 13 and 16 + 1 = 17. Hence 5 ★ 2 = 25 + 4 = 29.
Pointing to a boy, Meena says, "He is the son of the only son of my father's father." How is the boy related to Meena?
Cousin
Father
Nephew
Brother
The only son of Meena's paternal grandfather must be Meena's own father. The son of her father is her brother. Cousin would apply only if the grandfather had another son.
A man walks 6 km towards North, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
8 km East
8 km West
10 km North-East
14 km East
North 6 km, then East 8 km, then South 6 km. The north and south movements cancel out, leaving him 8 km due East of the starting point.
In a row of 40 children, Anu is 12th from the left end. What is her position from the right end?
28th
30th
29th
27th
Position from right = total − position from left + 1 = 40 − 12 + 1 = 29. Forgetting to add 1 gives the wrong answer 28th.
If 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 1 January 2026?
Wednesday
Friday
Thursday
Tuesday
2025 is not a leap year, so it has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. The same date next year moves one day forward, from Wednesday to Thursday.

Statements:
Some cats are dogs.
No dog is a rat.
Conclusions:
I. Some cats are not rats.
II. No cat is a rat.
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Only conclusion I follows
Neither I nor II follows
The cats that are dogs cannot be rats, so some cats are definitely not rats (I follows). Other cats may or may not be rats, so II is not certain.
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40?
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |90 − 220| = 130°. The hour hand moves 0.5° per minute, so it is not exactly on 3; ignoring this gives 150°.
How many times does the digit 7 appear when all the numbers from 1 to 100 are written?
7 appears in the units place 10 times (7, 17 … 97) and in the tens place 10 times (70–79). 77 counts twice, giving 20 in total.
If P > Q, Q ≥ R and R > S, which of the following is definitely true?
Q = S
P > S
R > P
S ≥ Q
Combining the statements gives P > Q ≥ R > S, so P > S is always true. Q is greater than S, so Q = S and S ≥ Q are false, and R > P is impossible.

Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing North. C sits in the middle. A sits to the immediate right of C. B sits at one of the extreme ends. D does not sit at an extreme end. E sits to the immediate right of A. Who sits at the extreme left end?
D
B
E
A
C is 3rd and A is 4th, so E is 5th (extreme right). B must take the other end, the 1st place, and D sits 2nd. Hence B is at the extreme left.

General Awareness.overview: General Awareness in SSC MTS checks broad static knowledge: Indian Polity (Constitution, Parliament, Fundamental Rights and Duties), Indian history and the freedom movement, Indian and world geography, everyday science (physics, chemistry, biology), basic economics and banking terms, art and culture, and sports. Static facts carry most of the marks, so revise standard textbooks such as NCERT summaries. Focus on important Articles and Amendments, key battles and dates, rivers and states, vitamins and diseases, SI units and classical dances, and keep a short list of commonly confused pairs.
questions: The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Indian Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment?
44th Amendment, 1978
52nd Amendment, 1985
42nd Amendment, 1976
73rd Amendment, 1992

The 42nd Amendment (1976), based on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations, inserted Part IV-A (Article 51A) listing Fundamental Duties. The 44th Amendment removed property from the Fundamental Rights.
Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection of life and personal liberty?
Article 14
Article 21
Article 19
Article 32
Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law. Article 14 deals with equality and Article 32 with constitutional remedies.
Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of the Indian Parliament?
Vice-President of India
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
President of India
Chairman of the Finance Commission
Under Article 108 the President summons a joint sitting, but it is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. The Vice-President chairs only the Rajya Sabha.
The Battle of Plassey, which helped establish British power in Bengal, was fought in which year?
Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757. The Battle of Buxar followed in 1764, and 1761 is the Third Battle of Panipat.
Which Harappan site is known for a dockyard, suggesting maritime trade?
Mohenjo-daro
Kalibangan
Lothal
Rakhigarhi
Lothal in Gujarat had a brick-lined dockyard linked to trade routes. Mohenjo-daro is famous for the Great Bath and Kalibangan for ploughed fields.
Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
Krishna
Narmada
Kaveri
Godavari
The Godavari, rising at Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and flowing into the Bay of Bengal, is the longest peninsular river and is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'.
The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
Bihar
Jharkhand
Chhattisgarh
Tripura
The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Bihar lies entirely north of it.
Scurvy is caused by the deficiency of which vitamin?
Vitamin A
Vitamin D
Vitamin K
Vitamin C
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed for collagen formation; its lack causes bleeding gums and scurvy. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets and Vitamin A deficiency night blindness.
What is the SI unit of electric current?
Volt
Ohm
Watt
Ampere
Electric current is measured in amperes, one of the seven SI base units. The volt measures potential difference, the ohm resistance and the watt power.
Which gas makes up the largest share of the Earth's atmosphere by volume?
Nitrogen
Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Argon
Nitrogen forms about 78% of dry air, oxygen about 21% and argon nearly 0.9%. Carbon dioxide is only a small fraction despite its importance for climate.
In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?
Mitochondria
Ribosome
Golgi apparatus
Chloroplast
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps sunlight to make food. Mitochondria release energy through respiration and are called the powerhouse of the cell.
In banking terminology, the 'repo rate' is the rate at which:
commercial banks lend to their most creditworthy customers
RBI borrows money from commercial banks
RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
banks pay interest on savings deposits
Under a repo, banks borrow from the Reserve Bank of India by selling securities with an agreement to repurchase them. RBI borrowing from banks is the reverse repo concept.
How many players of each team are on the court at a time in a standard game of kabaddi?
A kabaddi team fields seven players on court, with a few substitutes. Eleven is the number for cricket, hockey and football teams.
Kathakali, a classical dance form known for elaborate make-up and costumes, belongs to which state?
Tamil Nadu
Odisha
Manipur
Kerala
Kathakali comes from Kerala. Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Odissi from Odisha and Manipuri from Manipur.
Who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
Raja Ram Mohan Roy
Swami Dayananda Saraswati
Swami Vivekananda
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875 with the call 'Go back to the Vedas'. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj.

English Language.overview: English Language tests basic grammar and vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms, idioms and phrases, one-word substitution, spelling, error spotting, fill in the blanks (articles, prepositions, verbs, phrasal verbs), sentence improvement, active and passive voice, direct and indirect speech, and short reading comprehension. Revise subject–verb agreement rules (each, neither…nor, either…or), tense usage with since and for, and conditional sentences. Read short passages carefully and answer only from what is stated. Learning word lists with their opposites and practising narration and voice conversion rules gives quick, reliable marks.
questions: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT as used in: 'The region has abundant rainfall.'
Scarce
Tiny
Plentiful
Hidden
Abundant means existing in large quantities, so 'plentiful' is the synonym. 'Scarce' is its opposite, while 'tiny' and 'hidden' are unrelated.
Which word is opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT in: 'The bottle is made of transparent glass.'
Clear
Opaque
Bright
Glossy
Transparent means letting light pass through. Opaque means not letting light pass, so it is the antonym. 'Clear' is close to a synonym.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'to break the ice'.
To start a conversation in an uneasy situation
To end a long friendship
To act very rudely
To solve a difficult problem quickly and without any help
'To break the ice' means to say or do something that relieves tension and gets people talking, for example at the start of a meeting with strangers.
Select the one word for: 'A place where birds are kept'.
Apiary
Aquarium
Kennel
Aviary
An aviary is an enclosure for birds. An apiary is a place where bees are kept, an aquarium is for fish and a kennel is for dogs.
Which of the following words has the correct spelling?
Neccessary
Necessary
Necesary
Neccesary
The correct spelling is 'necessary' — one 'c' and double 's'. A common memory aid: one collar, two sleeves.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Each of the students / have submitted / the project on time.
Each of the students
the project on time
No error
have submitted
'Each of' takes a singular verb, so it should be 'has submitted'. The subject is 'each', not 'students'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
He has been living in Pune ______ 2018.
for
from
since
by
With the present perfect continuous, 'since' is used for a point of time (2018) and 'for' for a period of time (five years).

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb.
Neither the teacher nor the students ______ present at the meeting yesterday.
was
is
were
has been
With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Students' is plural and the time is past, so 'were' is correct.

Select the most appropriate improvement for the underlined part.
'If I was you', I would accept the offer.
If I were you
If I am you
If I had been you
No improvement
Imaginary or hypothetical conditions use the subjunctive 'were' for all subjects: 'If I were you, I would…'. Hence 'was' must be replaced.
Select the correct passive form of: The police have arrested the thief.
The thief has been arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.
The thief had been arrested by the police.
The thief is being arrested by the police.
Present perfect active ('have arrested') becomes present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle. The singular subject 'thief' takes 'has been arrested'.
Select the correct indirect form of: She said to me, "Please help me."
She said to me that please help me.
She requested me to help me.
She told me that I should please help her.
She requested me to help her.
A request in direct speech becomes 'requested + object + to-infinitive', and 'please' is dropped. The pronoun 'me' changes to 'her' to refer to the speaker.

Read the passage and answer the question.
Rainwater harvesting means collecting rain from rooftops and storing it in tanks or letting it soak into the ground. In many towns, groundwater levels have fallen because more water is pumped out than is replaced. Harvesting rain helps refill underground water and reduces flooding of streets during heavy showers.
According to the passage, why have groundwater levels fallen in many towns?
Rain has stopped falling in towns
More water is pumped out than is replaced
Rooftops absorb most of the rain
Streets are flooded during heavy showers every year
The passage clearly says groundwater has fallen 'because more water is pumped out than is replaced'. Flooding is mentioned only as a problem harvesting helps reduce.

Read the passage and answer the question.
The village library opened with just two shelves of donated books. Within a year, children were coming every evening, and their parents began borrowing newspapers. The librarian, a retired teacher, also started a weekly reading hour for those who could not read well.
Which word best describes the overall tone of the passage?
Critical
Encouraging
Sorrowful
Sarcastic
The passage describes a small library that grows and helps children and adults, so its tone is positive and encouraging. Nothing in it criticises, mourns or mocks anyone.
Pick the word opposite in meaning to HUMBLE in: 'Despite his success, he remained humble.'
Modest
Arrogant
Polite
Simple
Humble means modest and not proud. Arrogant means having an exaggerated sense of one's importance, so it is the antonym. 'Modest' is a synonym.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb.
The doctor advised him to ______ smoking.
give up
give in
give off
give away
'Give up' means to stop doing something. 'Give in' means to surrender, 'give off' means to emit (smell or heat) and 'give away' means to donate or reveal.

Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension.overview: Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension (VARC) is the first section of CAT. Most questions are based on reading passages of roughly 400 to 600 words on topics such as economics, science, philosophy and culture, testing main idea, inference, tone and the effect of new information. The remaining questions are verbal ability items, usually para-summary, para-jumbles and the odd sentence out, often answered by typing a number rather than choosing an option. Revise by reading varied long-form articles daily, summarising each paragraph in one line, and practising how to eliminate options that are too broad, too extreme or merely restate a detail.
questions:
Read the passage and answer the question.
