Before the railways, every town in Britain kept its own time, set by the sun at local noon. Bristol's clocks ran about ten minutes behind London's, and nobody minded, because few people travelled fast enough for the difference to matter. The railways changed this. A timetable listing departures in a dozen local times invited missed connections and, worse, collisions on single-track lines. Railway companies therefore adopted London time across their networks in the 1840s, and towns gradually followed, often reluctantly; some public clocks displayed two minute hands, one for local time and one for 'railway time'. Uniform time was not required by law until 1880. What looks today like a natural feature of the world was a commercial convenience that became a social habit long before it became a legal rule.

The primary purpose of the passage is to:
show that standard time began as a practical arrangement before it acquired legal force
argue that the railways caused most of the collisions recorded in nineteenth-century Britain
explain why Bristol resisted London time longer than other towns
describe how clocks with two minute hands were engineered
The passage traces uniform time from a railway convenience to a social habit and only later to law (1880). Collisions, Bristol and the dual-hand clocks are supporting details, not the main purpose.

Read the passage and answer the question.

Railway companies therefore adopted London time across their networks in the 1840s, and towns gradually followed, often reluctantly; some public clocks displayed two minute hands, one for local time and one for 'railway time'. Uniform time was not required by law until 1880. What looks today like a natural feature of the world was a commercial convenience that became a social habit long before it became a legal rule.

The reference to public clocks with two minute hands mainly serves to illustrate:
that Bristol's local time ran ahead of London's
a transition period when local and railway time existed side by side
the technical superiority of railway clocks over town clocks
the legal penalty for towns that kept local time

Two minute hands, one for local and one for railway time, show both systems in use at once while towns 'gradually followed, often reluctantly'. Bristol actually ran behind London, so the last option misreads the passage.

Read the passage and answer the question.

Bristol's clocks ran about ten minutes behind London's, and nobody minded, because few people travelled fast enough for the difference to matter. The railways changed this. Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
Most travellers before the railway era carried watches set to London time.
Collisions on single-track lines stopped completely once London time was adopted by the railways.
Before 1880, a British town could lawfully keep a time different from London's.
Local time was abandoned because it was shown to be astronomically inaccurate.

Since uniform time was not required by law until 1880, keeping local time earlier was lawful. The passage never claims collisions ended entirely, and local time was in fact astronomically accurate (set by the sun).

Read the passage and answer the question.

When employees must actively sign up for a pension plan, participation is often modest; when they are enrolled automatically and must actively opt out, participation rises sharply, even though the choice available to them is identical. Economists once explained such gaps by the cost of filling in forms, but the paperwork involved is usually trivial. A more persuasive account is that a default carries an implicit message: people read it as the option their employer, or the experts behind the plan, consider sensible. Inertia and procrastination then do the rest. This explains why defaults are powerful, and also why they can do harm. A default contribution rate set too low may anchor savers at that level for years, leaving them worse off than if they had been made to choose for themselves.

According to the passage, the 'cost of filling in forms' explanation is weak because:
employees rarely read the forms that their employers hand out at joining
procrastination has no effect on pension decisions
automatic enrolment removes any option of leaving the plan
the paperwork involved is usually too small to account for the gap

The author dismisses the form-cost explanation because 'the paperwork involved is usually trivial'. Automatic enrolment still allows opting out, and the passage says inertia and procrastination matter, so those options contradict it.

Read the passage and answer the question.

Economists once explained such gaps by the cost of filling in forms, but the paperwork involved is usually trivial. A more persuasive account is that a default carries an implicit message: people read it as the option their employer, or the experts behind the plan, consider sensible. Inertia and procrastination then do the rest. This explains why defaults are powerful, and also why they can do harm. A default contribution rate set too low may anchor savers at that level for years, leaving them worse off than if they had been made to choose for themselves.

The author's attitude towards default options is best described as:
neutral, because the passage never evaluates defaults at all
appreciative of their power but alert to their risks
dismissive, since defaults merely reflect the cost of paperwork
wholly enthusiastic about automatic enrolment in every form

The author says the account 'explains why defaults are powerful, and also why they can do harm', citing a low default rate that anchors savers. This balanced view rules out dismissive, wholly enthusiastic or neutral readings.

Read the passage and answer the question.

When employees must actively sign up for a pension plan, participation is often modest; when they are enrolled automatically and must actively opt out, participation rises sharply, even though the choice available to them is identical. Economists once explained such gaps by the cost of filling in forms, but the paperwork involved is usually trivial. A more persuasive account is that a default carries an implicit message: people read it as the option their employer, or the experts behind the plan, consider sensible. Inertia and procrastination then do the rest. This explains why defaults are powerful, and also why they can do harm. A default contribution rate set too low may anchor savers at that level for years, leaving them worse off than if they had been made to choose for themselves.

Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the 'implicit message' explanation?
Participation rises just as much when employees are told the default was picked at random.
Employees who opt out of the plan tend to earn more than those who stay enrolled in it.
Some firms set their default contribution rates higher than other firms do.
Many employees say they trust their employer's advice on money matters.

If a default known to be random works equally well, its power cannot come from people reading it as an expert endorsement. Trusting employer advice would strengthen the account; the other options are irrelevant to the mechanism.

Choose the option that best captures the essence of the paragraph.

Weather forecasts are often blamed when rain fails to arrive on a day marked '70 per cent chance of rain'. But such a forecast is not a promise; it means that on days with similar conditions, rain fell on about seven in ten. A forecaster whose 70 per cent days stay dry three times in ten is performing exactly as intended. Public frustration comes from reading a probability as a prediction about a single day.
People trusted forecasts more when they were stated in plain words.
Weather forecasts are unreliable, since rain falls on only seventy per cent of the days predicted.
A probabilistic forecast should be judged over many similar days, not by whether it came true on one day.
Forecasters should drop percentages and simply say whether it will rain.

The paragraph's point is that a 70 per cent forecast is correct if it rains on about 70 per cent of such days, so it must be judged in aggregate. It does not call forecasts unreliable or propose dropping percentages.

Choose the option that best captures the essence of the paragraph.

Much of the world's software rests on open-source libraries maintained by a handful of unpaid volunteers. Companies that earn billions from products built on these libraries rarely contribute money or staff time to them. When a maintainer burns out or a critical flaw goes unnoticed, the damage spreads far beyond the project itself. The arrangement works only as long as goodwill holds.
Open-source software is less secure than commercial software because volunteers write it.
Companies should stop using open-source libraries in products that earn revenue.
Most software flaws are caused by maintainers who are not paid.
Widely used open-source software rests on a thin, unpaid base of maintainers, making it more fragile than it appears.

The paragraph stresses dependence on a few unpaid maintainers and the wide damage if goodwill fails. It does not compare security with commercial software, prescribe abandoning open source, or blame most flaws on unpaid work.

Choose the option that best captures the essence of the paragraph.

A museum label once told visitors what an object was, where it came from and who made it. Increasingly, labels also explain how the object reached the museum: whether it was bought, gifted, or taken during war or colonial rule. Some curators see this as a distraction from the object itself; others argue that the journey is part of the object's meaning. Either way, the label has become a site of argument rather than a neutral caption.
By addressing how objects were acquired, museum labels have turned from neutral captions into contested statements.
Museums should return every object that was taken during war or colonial rule.
Visitors spend more time reading labels than looking at objects.
Curators now agree that an object's acquisition history matters more than the object itself.

The paragraph describes labels adding acquisition history and curators disagreeing about it, so labels have become contested. Curators are said to disagree, not agree, and the paragraph makes no recommendation about returning objects.

The four sentences below, when properly sequenced, form a coherent paragraph. Choose the correct order.

1. This is why engineers have begun testing it as a substitute for steel reinforcement in low-cost buildings.
2. Bamboo is technically a grass, yet some species grow nearly a metre in a single day.
3. Its strength, too, is remarkable: weight for weight, certain species rival mild steel in tension.
4. Such rapid growth makes it one of the most renewable building materials available.

Sentence 2 introduces bamboo; 4 ('Such rapid growth') follows it. Sentence 3 adds a second quality with 'too', and 1 ('This is why') draws the conclusion from both renewability and strength. Hence 2-4-3-1.

The four sentences below, when properly sequenced, form a coherent paragraph. Choose the correct order.

1. In them, merchants exchanged shipping news, and some became the seeds of insurance markets and stock exchanges.
2. Coffee houses spread rapidly through London in the late seventeenth century.
3. Unlike taverns, they offered a sober setting where strangers could talk for the price of a cup.
4. Lloyd's of London, for example, began in a coffee house run by Edward Lloyd.

Sentence 2 opens the topic; 3 describes what coffee houses offered ('they'); 1 ('In them') explains their commercial role; 4 gives Lloyd's as an example of an insurance market born there. Hence 2-3-1-4.

The four sentences below, when properly sequenced, form a coherent paragraph. Choose the correct order.

1. In experiments, pigeons fitted with small magnets lost their way when released under overcast skies.
2. On sunny days, however, the same birds homed correctly, apparently by using the sun.
3. Homing pigeons appear to be able to sense the Earth's magnetic field.
4. They thus seem to carry more than one compass and use whichever is available.

Sentence 3 states the claim; 1 gives the magnet experiment; 2 contrasts sunny days with 'however' and 'the same birds'; 4 concludes with 'thus'. Placing 2 before 1 would leave 'the same birds' without a referent.

Four of the five sentences below can be arranged into a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does NOT fit.

1. Fermentation was used to preserve food long before anyone understood the microbes responsible.
2. Yoghurt, idli batter and sauerkraut all depend on bacteria that turn sugars into acids.
3. The acidity they produce makes the food hostile to many organisms that cause spoilage.
4. Refrigerators became common in Indian middle-class homes only in the late twentieth century.
5. Ancient cooks thus harnessed microbiology without knowing it existed.
Sentence 5
Sentence 1
Sentence 4
Sentence 2
Sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5 form a chain on fermentation as unknowing use of microbes. Sentence 4 shifts to the spread of refrigerators, a different preservation story, and breaks that chain.

Four of the five sentences below can be arranged into a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does NOT fit.

1. Early chess programs relied on searching millions of positions using rules written by human experts.
2. Newer engines instead learn by playing millions of games against themselves.
3. Chess is believed to have originated in India as chaturanga around the sixth century.
4. Some of their moves, once dismissed as errors, are now studied closely by grandmasters.
5. The shift has changed not only how machines play but how humans understand the game.
Sentence 1
Sentence 4
Sentence 5
Sentence 3
Sentences 1, 2, 4 and 5 describe the shift from rule-based to self-taught engines and its effect on human play. The origin of chess in India is unrelated to that argument.

Four of the five sentences below can be arranged into a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does NOT fit.

1. Trials of a four-day working week have reported stable output alongside lower staff turnover.
2. Critics point out that most trials involved firms that volunteered, and so were likely to succeed.
3. Results from self-selected participants may not hold when a policy is applied across an economy.
4. Supporters respond that even self-selected trials show the idea works in some sectors.
5. Productivity growth in many economies slowed after the 2008 financial crisis.
Sentence 5
Sentence 2
Sentence 4
Sentence 3
Sentences 1-2-3-4 form a debate: trial results, a selection-bias critique, its implication, and the supporters' reply. The general post-2008 productivity slowdown does not belong to this exchange.

Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning.overview: Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning (DILR) in CAT is built around sets: a table, chart or puzzle followed by several questions. Typical sets include arrangements, scheduling, tournaments, selections with conditions, games, Venn-type counting and data tables needing percentage or ratio work. Accuracy matters more than attempting every set, so the key skill is choosing which sets to solve. When practising, draw clear grids, list every condition, test cases systematically, and keep quick mental tools for percentage change, averages and ratios ready.
questions:
Quarterly sales (units) of four products:
Product | Q1 | Q2 | Q3
A | 240 | 300 | 330
B | 180 | 216 | 270
C | 300 | 270 | 324
D | 150 | 195 | 210

Which product recorded the highest percentage growth in sales from Q1 to Q3?
C
B
D
A
Growth Q1 to Q3: A 90/240 = 37.5%, B 90/180 = 50%, C 24/300 = 8%, D 60/150 = 40%. B leads even though A has the same absolute increase of 90 units.

Quarterly sales (units) of four products:
Product | Q1 | Q2 | Q3
A | 240 | 300 | 330
B | 180 | 216 | 270
C | 300 | 270 | 324
D | 150 | 195 | 210

By approximately what percentage did the combined sales of the four products rise from Q1 to Q2?

Quarterly sales (units) of four products:
Product | Q1 | Q2 | Q3
A | 240 | 300 | 330
B | 180 | 216 | 270
C | 300 | 270 | 324
D | 150 | 195 | 210

For how many products did sales increase in BOTH transitions, Q1 to Q2 and Q2 to Q3?
A, B and D rise in both quarters. C falls from 300 to 270 in Q2 before recovering to 324, so it does not qualify. Answer: 3.

Employees of a company by department:
Department | Employees | Women (%)
HR | 80 | 45
Sales | 250 | 32
Tech | 400 | 25
Finance | 120 | 40
Ops | 150 | 20

How many women work in the company in total?
Women: HR 36, Sales 80, Tech 100, Finance 48, Ops 30. Total = 294, which is 29.4% of the 1,000 employees.

Employees of a company by department:
Department | Employees | Women (%)
HR | 80 | 45
Sales | 250 | 32
Tech | 400 | 25
Finance | 120 | 40
Ops | 150 | 20

What is the ratio of men in Sales to men in Finance?
Men in Sales = 250 − 80 = 170; men in Finance = 120 − 48 = 72. Ratio 170 : 72 = 85 : 36. 25 : 12 wrongly compares total employees.

Six friends G, H, I, J, K and L sit in a row facing north in seats 1 to 6 (seat 1 is at the extreme left).
• J and H sit at the two ends.
• H sits immediately to the right of K.
• Exactly two people sit between I and J.
• L is not adjacent to I.
• G sits somewhere to the left of K.

Who sits in seat 3?
K
L
I
G
J and H take the ends and K is immediately left of H, so H is at 6, K at 5, J at 1. I is three seats from J, at 4. L cannot be next to I, so L is at 2 and G at 3.

Six friends G, H, I, J, K and L sit in a row facing north in seats 1 to 6 (seat 1 is at the extreme left).
• J and H sit at the two ends.
• H sits immediately to the right of K.
• Exactly two people sit between I and J.
• L is not adjacent to I.
• G sits somewhere to the left of K.

How many people sit between L and K?
The only valid arrangement from left is J, L, G, I, K, H. L is in seat 2 and K in seat 5, so G and I sit between them: two people.

A committee of exactly three is to be chosen from P, Q, R, S, T and U, subject to:
• P and Q cannot both be chosen.
• If R is chosen, S must be chosen.
• T can be chosen only if U is chosen.
How many different committees are possible?
Listing valid sets: PRS, PSU, PTU, QRS, QSU, QTU, RSU, STU. Any set with R but not S, T but not U, or both P and Q is excluded, leaving 8.

One of four suspects A, B, C and D broke a window. Exactly one of the following statements is true.
A: "B did it."
B: "D did it."
C: "I did not do it."
D: "B is lying."
Who broke the window?
C
B
D
A
B's and D's statements contradict, so exactly one of them is true. Hence A and C are both false. C's statement being false means C did it; then B is false and D is true, as required.

On a grid of streets, Rina walks from corner (0, 0) to corner (4, 3), moving only one block east or one block north at a time. The corner (2, 1) is closed. How many different shortest routes can she take?
All shortest routes: C(7,3) = 35. Routes through (2,1): C(3,1) × C(4,2) = 3 × 6 = 18. Routes avoiding it = 35 − 18 = 17.
If 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 1 January 2029?
Monday
Tuesday
Saturday
Sunday
From 2025 to 2028 there are 3 ordinary years (1 odd day each) and the leap year 2028 (2 odd days): 5 odd days. Wednesday + 5 = Monday.
Five students scored whole-number marks (out of 100) in a test. The average is 72, the median is 75, and 80 is the only mode. What is the highest possible value of the lowest score?
Since 80 must appear at least twice and exceed the median, the top two scores are 80 and 80. The lowest two sum to 360 − 75 − 160 = 125 and must differ, so the best split is 62 and 63.
There are 10 identical-looking coins, one of which is slightly heavier. Using only a two-pan balance, what is the minimum number of weighings that guarantees finding the heavier coin?
Each weighing has three outcomes, so k weighings separate at most 3^k coins. 3² = 9 < 10 ≤ 27 = 3³, so three weighings are needed and suffice.
A shop's monthly sales (₹ lakh) for January to May were 48, 55, 42, 60 and 51. The average for January to June was ₹52 lakh. In how many of the six months were sales above the six-month average?
June = 6 × 52 − (48+55+42+60+51) = 312 − 256 = 56. Months above 52: February (55), April (60) and June (56), i.e. three months.

Five boxes V, W, X, Y and Z are stacked one above another (position 1 is the bottom).
• X is somewhere above W.
• Exactly one box lies between Y and X.
• Z is directly above V.
• W is not at the bottom.
• Y is not at the top.
• V is not at the bottom.

Which box is at the top?
W
X
Y
Z
Testing placements, the only arrangement meeting all conditions from bottom to top is Y, W, X, V, Z. Z sits directly on V at the top, X is above W, and exactly one box (W) lies between Y and X.

Quantitative Ability.overview: Quantitative Ability (QA) in CAT covers arithmetic (percentages, profit and loss, interest, ratio, mixtures, time-speed-distance, time and work), algebra (equations, inequalities, functions, progressions, logarithms), geometry and mensuration, number system, and modern maths such as permutations, combinations and probability. Arithmetic and algebra usually carry the most weight. Revise core formulas, but focus on approaches that save time: working with ratios instead of raw values, checking options by substitution, and recognising standard patterns like cyclicity of remainders or the inclusion-exclusion principle.
questions: A sum of money lent at compound interest (compounded annually) amounts to ₹13,310 in 3 years and ₹14,641 in 4 years. What is the sum?
Ratio of successive amounts 14,641/13,310 = 1.1, so the rate is 10%. Principal = 13,310 / 1.1³ = 13,310 / 1.331 = ₹10,000.
Two runners start together from the same point on a circular track and run in opposite directions at 5 m/s and 7 m/s. At how many distinct points on the track will they meet?
For runners moving in opposite directions with speeds in the lowest ratio a : b, the number of distinct meeting points is a + b = 5 + 7 = 12. Running in the same direction would give |a − b| = 2.
A vessel holds 80 litres of a 30% acid solution. How many litres of pure acid must be added to raise the concentration to 50%?
Acid now = 24 L. Adding x L: (24 + x)/(80 + x) = 0.5, so 48 + 2x = 80 + x and x = 32. Check: 56/112 = 50%.
A and B together can finish a job in 10 days, B and C in 15 days, and A and C in 12 days. How long will A, B and C take working together?
6 days
7.5 days
8 days
9 days
Adding pair rates: 2(A + B + C) = 1/10 + 1/15 + 1/12 = 15/60 = 1/4. So A + B + C = 1/8 per day, i.e. 8 days together.
Find the remainder left on dividing 2²⁰²⁶ by 7.
2³ = 8 leaves remainder 1 on division by 7, so powers of 2 repeat in a cycle of 3 (2, 4, 1). Since 2026 = 3 × 675 + 1, 2²⁰²⁶ leaves the same remainder as 2¹, which is 2.
How many ordered triples of positive integers (x, y, z) satisfy x + y + z = 12?
By stars and bars, positive solutions of x + y + z = n number C(n − 1, 2). For n = 12 this is C(11, 2) = 55. C(12, 2) = 66 would count non-negative solutions of x + y + z = 11 instead.
The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression is 3n² + 5n. What is its 10th term?
T₁₀ = S₁₀ − S₉ = (300 + 50) − (243 + 45) = 350 − 288 = 62. In general Tₙ = 6n + 2, so the common difference is 6.
What is the radius of the circle inscribed in a right-angled triangle whose legs are 9 cm and 12 cm?
3 cm
2.5 cm
4 cm
6 cm
The hypotenuse is 15 cm. For a right triangle, inradius r = (a + b − c)/2 = (9 + 12 − 15)/2 = 3 cm. Equivalently, area 54 divided by semi-perimeter 18 gives 3.
A number is picked at random from 1 to 50. What is the probability that it is divisible by 3 or by 5?
Multiples of 3: 16; of 5: 10; of 15: 3. By inclusion-exclusion, 16 + 10 − 3 = 23 favourable numbers, so the probability is 23/50.
How many integers x satisfy |2x − 5| < 9?
−9 < 2x − 5 < 9 gives −4 < 2x < 14, i.e. −2 < x < 7. The integers are −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: eight values.
If f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² − 1, what is f(g(2)) − g(f(1))?
g(2) = 3, so f(g(2)) = 9. f(1) = 5, so g(f(1)) = 24. The difference is 9 − 24 = −15; reversing the order of composition gives the tempting 15.
A shopkeeper marks an item 40% above cost and then allows two successive discounts of 10% each. What is his profit percentage?
Selling price = 1.40 × 0.90 × 0.90 = 1.134 times cost, so profit is 13.4%. Subtracting 20% from 40% ignores that the second discount applies to an already reduced price.
A wooden cuboid measuring 12 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm is cut into identical cubes of the largest possible size with no wood wasted. How many cubes are obtained?
The largest cube edge is HCF(12, 8, 6) = 2 cm. Number of cubes = (12/2) × (8/2) × (6/2) = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72.
Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010, how many digits does 2⁵⁰ have?
log₁₀(2⁵⁰) = 50 × 0.3010 = 15.05. A number whose logarithm has integer part 15 has 15 + 1 = 16 digits.
A train passes a 200 m platform in 20 seconds and overtakes a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train?
Let speed be v m/s and length L. L + 200 = 20v and L = 12(v − 5/3). So 20v − 200 = 12v − 20, giving v = 22.5 m/s and L = 250 m.

Quantitative Techniques & Data Interpret.overview: This section tests arithmetic and data handling under time pressure: percentages, profit and loss, discounts, ratio and mixtures, time and work, pipes, speed and distance, simple and compound interest, mensuration, permutations, probability and short data-interpretation sets based on tables or charts. Revise the core formulas, practise converting fractions to percentages quickly, and learn shortcuts such as CI − SI for two years and the equal-distance average-speed formula. In DI sets, read units and base years carefully before calculating, and approximate where the options are far apart.
questions: An article has a marked price of ₹2,500. The shopkeeper allows successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the selling price?
After 20% off, the price is ₹2,000; a further 10% off gives ₹1,800. Successive discounts of 20% and 10% equal a single discount of 28%, not 30%.
A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
6 days
9 days
10 days
8 days
Together they do 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day, so 20/36 = 5/9 in 4 days. The remaining 4/9 at B's rate of 1/18 per day takes 8 days.
A 240-metre-long train passes a signal pole in 12 seconds. How long will it take to cross a platform 360 metres long?
30 seconds
18 seconds
24 seconds
36 seconds
Speed = 240 ÷ 12 = 20 m/s. To cross the platform the train covers its own length plus the platform, 600 m, which takes 600 ÷ 20 = 30 seconds.
What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹12,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum?
For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 12,000 × 0.01 = ₹120. The extra amount is simply interest earned in year two on the first year's interest of ₹1,200.
If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 7, what is A : B : C?
Make B common: 3:4 becomes 9:12 and 6:7 becomes 12:14. Hence A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 14. Simply joining 3:4 and 7 ignores the different values of B.
Pipe X fills a tank in 20 minutes and pipe Y in 30 minutes, while outlet Z empties the full tank in 15 minutes. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill it?
60 minutes
12 minutes
36 minutes
45 minutes
Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/15 = (3 + 2 − 4)/60 = 1/60 of the tank per minute, so the tank fills in 60 minutes.
A trader sells a watch at a loss of 15%. Had he sold it for ₹360 more, he would have made a profit of 9%. What is the cost price of the watch?
The gap between −15% and +9% is 24% of the cost price, which equals ₹360. So CP = 360 ÷ 0.24 = ₹1,500.
A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 5. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1 : 1?
5 litres
10 litres
12 litres
15 litres
The mixture has 35 litres of milk and 25 litres of water. For equal quantities, water must also be 35 litres, so 10 litres must be added.

Annual sales of a company (₹ crore): 2019 – 120, 2020 – 150, 2021 – 135, 2022 – 180, 2023 – 198.
In which year was the percentage growth in sales over the previous year the highest?
Growth: 2020 = 25%, 2021 = −10%, 2022 = 45/135 ≈ 33.3%, 2023 = 10%. Although 2020 rose by ₹30 crore too, 2022's rise came on a smaller base.

Annual sales of a company (₹ crore): 2019 – 120, 2020 – 150, 2021 – 135, 2022 – 180, 2023 – 198.
What were the average annual sales over the five years?
₹150.0 crore
₹156.6 crore
₹159.0 crore
₹162.4 crore
Total sales = 120 + 150 + 135 + 180 + 198 = ₹783 crore. Dividing by 5 years gives an average of ₹156.6 crore.
Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 8?
Favourable outcomes are (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3) and (6,2): five out of 36 equally likely outcomes, so the probability is 5/36.
In how many distinct ways can the letters of the word LEADER be arranged?
LEADER has 6 letters with E repeated twice. Number of arrangements = 6! ÷ 2! = 720 ÷ 2 = 360. Using 720 ignores the repetition.
A car travels from town P to town Q at 40 km/h and returns along the same road at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
50 km/h
45 km/h
52 km/h
48 km/h
For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 ÷ 100 = 48 km/h. The simple average of 50 km/h is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed.
A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest. In how many years will it become 8 times itself at the same rate?
20 years
40 years
15 years
10 years
Under compounding, the sum multiplies by 2 every 5 years: 2 → 4 → 8 takes three such periods, i.e. 15 years. The answer 40 years would apply to simple interest.
What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
440 cm³
Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 10 = 1,540 cm³. The value 440 is the curved surface area (2πrh), not the volume.

Logical Reasoning.overview: Logical Reasoning covers number and letter series, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions, ranking, seating arrangements, syllogisms, inequalities, calendars and clocks, analogies, odd-one-out and critical reasoning such as strengthening or weakening an argument. Draw quick diagrams for seating and family trees, use Venn diagrams for syllogisms, and learn standard formulas for clock angles and odd days. In critical-reasoning items, look for the assumption linking evidence to conclusion; an alternative explanation usually weakens a causal claim.
questions:
Find the next term of the series.
3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
The terms are n² − 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, so the next is 7² − 1 = 48. Equivalently, the differences 5, 7, 9, 11 continue with 13.

Find the next letter in the series.
B, E, I, N, ?
S
T
U
R
Positions are 2, 5, 9, 14: the gaps increase 3, 4, 5, so the next gap is 6, giving position 20, which is T.
In a certain code, TEACHER is written as VGCEJGT. How will STUDENT be written in that code?
UVWEGPV
TUVFGPV
UWVFGPV
UVWFGPV
Each letter is shifted two places forward: T→V, E→G, A→C and so on. Applying +2 to STUDENT gives U V W F G P V.
Pointing to a young man, Riya says, "He is the son of the only son of my grandfather." Assuming Riya's grandfather is her paternal grandfather, how is the man related to Riya?
Brother
Cousin
Uncle
Nephew
The only son of Riya's paternal grandfather is her father. The son of her father is her brother. A cousin would need the grandfather to have another child.
Arun is facing east. He turns 90° clockwise, then 180°, and then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
East
North
West
South
East turned 90° clockwise is South; turning 180° gives North; turning 90° anticlockwise from North gives West.
In a class of 45 students, Mohan ranks 12th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
33rd
35th
34th
32nd
Rank from bottom = total − rank from top + 1 = 45 − 12 + 1 = 34. Forgetting to add 1 gives 33rd, a common slip.

Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B is immediately to the right of A. C sits opposite B. E is not adjacent to A. Who sits immediately to the left of A?
F
E
C
D
B is on A's right and E cannot touch A, so F must be on A's left. Then C opposite B and D opposite A leave E between B and D.

Statements:
All pens are books.
No book is a table.
Conclusions:
I. No pen is a table.
II. Some tables are pens.
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Neither I nor II follows
Every pen lies inside 'books', and books share nothing with tables, so no pen can be a table. Conclusion II directly contradicts I, so it cannot follow.

Statement: P > Q ≥ R = S < T
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. T > Q
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both I and II follow
Either I or II follows
From P > Q ≥ R = S we get P > S, so I is true. T and Q are both only linked to S, and both are at least S, so their mutual order cannot be fixed.
If 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 1 January 2026?
Wednesday
Friday
Tuesday
Thursday
2025 is not a leap year, so it has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. The weekday therefore moves forward by one, from Wednesday to Thursday.
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40?
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |90 − 220| = 130°. The hour hand moves too, so it is not simply the 120° between the 4 and 8 marks.
The traffic police of a city claim that speed cameras installed in January reduced road accidents by 30% during that year. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this claim?
A new metro line opened in the same January and took many cars off the roads
The cameras were installed mainly on roads with the highest accident rates in the city
Drivers caught by the cameras had to pay fines that were higher than in earlier years
Accidents also fell in areas where the speed cameras were operating round the clock

An alternative cause that coincides in time, the metro line reducing traffic, could explain the fall in accidents, so the cameras may not be responsible. The other options either fit or support the claim.

Find the missing number.
7 : 50 :: 9 : ?
The relation is n² + 1: 7² + 1 = 50, so 9² + 1 = 82. Choosing 81 forgets the +1 step.

Which one does NOT belong to the group?
Mercury, Venus, Mars, Moon
Mercury
Venus
Mars
Moon
Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets orbiting the Sun. The Moon is a natural satellite orbiting the Earth, so it is the odd one out.
Among five friends A, B, C, D and E, A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is shorter than B, and E is taller than C. Who is the third tallest?
B
C
A
E
Combining the clues gives E > C > A > B > D. Counting from the tallest, A is third. C is second, and B is fourth.

Language Comprehension.overview: Language Comprehension tests vocabulary, grammar and reading. Expect synonyms and antonyms, idioms, one-word substitution, error spotting, fill-in-the-blanks, sentence improvement, para jumbles and short reading passages with questions on the main idea, details and inference. Revise subject–verb agreement, conditionals, prepositions and comparatives such as 'senior to'. Build vocabulary through regular reading. For passages, read the questions first, then identify the author's central claim, and reject options that are too extreme or contradict the text.
questions:
Her candid feedback, though uncomfortable, helped the team improve.
Which word is closest in meaning to CANDID as used here?
Secretive
Cautious
Cunning
Frank
Candid means honest and straightforward in speech, which is what frank means. Secretive and cunning suggest concealment, the opposite idea.

The firm hired temporary staff to augment its sales force before the festive season.
Which word is the antonym of AUGMENT?
Enlarge
Supplement
Diminish
Amplify
To augment is to increase or add to something. Diminish means to reduce, so it is the antonym; the other three are near-synonyms of augment.

The auditor was meticulous, checking every voucher twice.
Choose the synonym of METICULOUS.
Careless
Painstaking
Hurried
Ambitious
A meticulous person pays very careful attention to every detail, which is the sense of painstaking. Careless and hurried are opposites.
Choose the one word for: a person who does not believe in the existence of God.
Atheist
Agnostic
Theist
Heretic
An atheist denies the existence of God. An agnostic holds that it cannot be known, a theist believes, and a heretic holds views opposed to accepted doctrine.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'a blessing in disguise'.
A gift that is given secretly to someone in need
Something that seems bad at first but turns out well
A favour that later causes serious trouble
A hidden talent that nobody has noticed yet
A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that later proves beneficial, for example losing a job that leads to a better one.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom 'to bell the cat'.
To raise a false alarm in order to scare people
To reveal a secret that one promised to keep
To keep a constant watch over a dishonest person
To take on a risky task for the benefit of others
From the fable of the mice who wanted a bell on the cat but found no volunteer, to bell the cat means to undertake a dangerous job on everyone's behalf.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither the manager nor his assistants / was present / at the meeting / yesterday.
was present
Neither the manager nor his assistants
at the meeting
yesterday
With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Assistants' is plural, so the sentence needs 'were present'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
He is senior than me / in the organisation, / but he never / behaves arrogantly.
in the organisation,
but he never
He is senior than me
behaves arrogantly.
Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and prior take 'to', not 'than'. The correct form is 'He is senior to me'.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
Despite repeated reminders, the vendor remained ______ about the delivery date and gave no clear answer.
punctual
transparent
evasive
grateful
'Despite repeated reminders' and 'gave no clear answer' signal avoidance, so evasive fits. Transparent would mean the opposite, being open and clear.

Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.
She has been working with this firm ______ 2019.
since
for
from
by
'Since' is used with a point in time in the present perfect continuous. 'For' is used with a period, such as 'for six years'.

Select the best replacement for the underlined part. If no improvement is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
[If I would have known] about the delay, I would have taken the earlier train.
If I knew
If I would know
No improvement
Had I known
A third conditional uses the past perfect in the if-clause: 'If I had known' or the inverted 'Had I known'. 'Would have' never appears in the if-clause.

Arrange the sentences into a coherent paragraph.
P. As a result, even small shops now accept payments through a phone.
Q. Over the past decade, digital payments in India have grown rapidly.
R. This growth has been driven largely by the Unified Payments Interface.
S. UPI allows instant transfers between bank accounts at little or no cost.
QSRP
QRSP
RQSP
QRPS
Q introduces the topic, R names the driver of growth, S explains what UPI does, and P gives the consequence ('As a result'). So the order is QRSP.

Read the passage and answer the question.

When companies first moved to remote work, many managers feared that productivity would collapse. For routine, well-defined tasks, the fear proved largely unfounded: output held steady and employees saved hours of commuting. The harder problems were subtler. New hires, who learn much by watching experienced colleagues, found it difficult to absorb the informal knowledge that never appears in a manual. Spontaneous conversations that spark ideas also became rarer. Firms that succeeded did not simply return everyone to the office; they deliberately created occasions for mentoring and unstructured interaction, whether in person or online.

Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
Remote work's real cost was lost informal learning, which firms had to address deliberately
Remote work sharply reduced the output of employees doing routine and well-defined tasks
Companies should bring all employees back to the office to restore their productivity
Saving commuting time is the most important benefit that remote work offers to staff

The passage says routine output held steady; the subtler problem was weaker informal learning and fewer spontaneous ideas, which successful firms tackled on purpose. It rejects a simple return to office.

Read the passage and answer the question.

When companies first moved to remote work, many managers feared that productivity would collapse. For routine, well-defined tasks, the fear proved largely unfounded: output held steady and employees saved hours of commuting. The harder problems were subtler. New hires, who learn much by watching experienced colleagues, found it difficult to absorb the informal knowledge that never appears in a manual. Spontaneous conversations that spark ideas also became rarer. Firms that succeeded did not simply return everyone to the office; they deliberately created occasions for mentoring and unstructured interaction, whether in person or online.

According to the passage, which group found remote work especially difficult?
Senior managers
New hires
Employees doing routine tasks
Workers with long commutes
The passage states that new hires, who learn by watching experienced colleagues, struggled to absorb informal knowledge. Routine-task employees, by contrast, kept output steady.

Read the passage and answer the question.

When companies first moved to remote work, many managers feared that productivity would collapse. For routine, well-defined tasks, the fear proved largely unfounded: output held steady and employees saved hours of commuting. The harder problems were subtler. New hires, who learn much by watching experienced colleagues, found it difficult to absorb the informal knowledge that never appears in a manual. Spontaneous conversations that spark ideas also became rarer. Firms that succeeded did not simply return everyone to the office; they deliberately created occasions for mentoring and unstructured interaction, whether in person or online.

With which statement would the author most likely agree?
Productivity always falls when employees stop meeting in person
Formal manuals capture nearly everything a new employee needs
Online interaction cannot support any kind of mentoring at all
Returning all staff to the office is not, by itself, a complete solution
The author says successful firms 'did not simply return everyone to the office' and created mentoring 'in person or online'. Hence an office return alone is not enough.

General Awareness.overview: General Awareness in CMAT covers static GK and business-related awareness: the Indian Constitution and polity, history, geography, basic science, economic concepts, banking terminology, and international organisations and their headquarters, along with recent developments. Focus first on stable facts that recur, such as key Articles, landmark events and dates, RBI instruments like repo, CRR and SLR, and concepts such as inflation and fiscal deficit. Make short revision lists, and update current affairs from reliable sources in the months before the exam.
questions: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty?
Article 14
Article 19
Article 21
Article 32
Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Article 14 deals with equality before law.
Which Article did Dr B. R. Ambedkar describe as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
Article 21
Article 226
Article 368
Article 32
Article 32, the Right to Constitutional Remedies, lets citizens move the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights. Article 226 gives similar but wider writ powers to High Courts.
What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha permitted by the Constitution?
The Constitution allows up to 250 members: 238 representatives of states and union territories plus 12 nominated by the President. 245 is the present actual strength.
Which is the largest state of India by area?
Madhya Pradesh
Rajasthan
Maharashtra
Uttar Pradesh
Rajasthan is the largest state by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. Uttar Pradesh is the largest by population, not area.
The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of these states?
Odisha
Gujarat
Jharkhand
Mizoram
The Tropic of Cancer crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies entirely south of it.
The repo rate is the rate at which:
banks lend money to their most creditworthy corporate customers
the RBI lends short-term funds to banks against government securities
the RBI borrows money from commercial banks by selling securities
banks pay interest to customers on their savings account deposits
Under a repo, banks borrow from the RBI by selling securities with an agreement to repurchase them. When the RBI absorbs funds from banks, that is a reverse repo or SDF operation.
Under the RBI's flexible inflation targeting framework, the inflation target is defined in terms of which index?
Wholesale Price Index
GDP deflator
Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
Consumer Price Index (Combined)
Since the framework was formalised in 2016, the target is set using headline CPI (Combined) inflation, which reflects retail prices across rural and urban India, rather than the WPI.
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through which Constitutional Amendment Act?
101st Amendment Act, 2016
73rd Amendment Act, 1992
86th Amendment Act, 2002
103rd Amendment Act, 2019
The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 enabled GST and created the GST Council (Article 279A); GST came into force on 1 July 2017. The 73rd concerns panchayats.
Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
Vitamin A
Vitamin D
Vitamin C
Vitamin K
Scurvy, marked by bleeding gums and weakness, results from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, and vitamin A deficiency night blindness.
What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
Volt
Ampere
Ohm
Watt
Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω). By Ohm's law, R = V/I, so one ohm is one volt per ampere. Volt measures potential difference and watt measures power.
The Battle of Plassey, which laid the foundation of British political power in Bengal, was fought in:
Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757. The Battle of Buxar (1764) later secured the diwani; 1761 was the Third Battle of Panipat.
Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March, which launched the Civil Disobedience Movement, began in which year?
The Salt March started from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi in April. 1920 marks Non-Cooperation and 1942 the Quit India Movement.
Where are the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) located?
New York
Washington, D.C.
Geneva
Paris
The IMF, like the World Bank, is headquartered in Washington, D.C. Geneva hosts the WTO and Paris the OECD, which are common distractors.
'Stagflation' refers to an economic situation in which:
high inflation coexists with stagnant growth and high unemployment
prices fall steadily while output and employment keep rising
rapid growth leads to full employment and low inflation
the government balances its budget during a recession
Stagflation combines rising prices with weak output and high unemployment, as in many economies in the 1970s. It is hard to tackle because anti-inflation measures can deepen the slowdown.
Under the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), a scheduled commercial bank must keep a specified share of its net demand and time liabilities:
in gold and approved securities with itself
as a cash balance with the RBI
as loans to priority-sector borrowers
as fixed deposits with NABARD
CRR is held as cash balance with the RBI and earns no interest. Holding liquid assets such as gold, cash and government securities with the bank itself is the SLR requirement.

Innovation & Entrepreneurship.overview: Innovation & Entrepreneurship tests the ideas and vocabulary of starting and growing ventures: types of innovation, lean startup concepts such as the MVP and pivot, business models and the Business Model Canvas, funding stages, burn rate and dilution, intellectual property (patents, copyright, designs, trademarks, trade secrets, GIs), and Indian startup-support initiatives. Learn standard definitions with examples, know the key thinkers such as Schumpeter, Christensen and Osterwalder, and practise short numerical questions on runway and equity stakes.
questions: In the Lean Startup approach, a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is best described as:
the cheapest product a firm can sell at a profit in the mass market
a fully featured product launched only after detailed market research
a prototype that is shown only to investors before any funding round
the simplest version of a product that lets the team learn from real customers
Eric Ries defines the MVP as the version that allows maximum validated learning about customers with the least effort. Its purpose is learning, not a polished or cheapest launch.
A food-delivery startup finds that offices, not households, are its most loyal customers, and reshapes its model to serve corporate canteens. In startup terminology, this is a:
Spin-off
Merger
Pivot
Bootstrap
A pivot is a structured change of strategy to test a new hypothesis while keeping what has been learned. A spin-off creates a separate company; bootstrapping concerns self-funding.
Under the Copyright Act, 1957, copyright in a published literary work generally lasts for:
20 years from publication
the author's lifetime plus 70 years
10 years, renewable every 10 years
the author's lifetime plus 60 years
In India, copyright in literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works lasts for the author's life plus 60 years. Life plus 70 years is the rule in the EU and USA, not India.
In India, registration of an industrial design under the Designs Act, 2000 gives protection for a maximum of:
10 years
20 years
15 years
60 years
Design registration is valid for 10 years and can be extended once by 5 years, giving 15 years in all. 20 years is the patent term.
The phrase 'creative destruction', describing how innovation replaces old industries, is most closely associated with:
Peter Drucker
Joseph Schumpeter
Adam Smith
Michael Porter
Schumpeter argued that entrepreneurs drive economic change through innovations that destroy existing products and firms. Drucker wrote on systematic innovation, and Porter on competitive strategy.
How many building blocks does the Business Model Canvas developed by Alexander Osterwalder contain?
Nine
Five
Seven
Twelve
The canvas has nine blocks: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships and cost structure.
Which sequence shows the usual order of startup funding stages?
Seed → Pre-seed → Series A → Series B
Pre-seed → Seed → Series A → Series B
Series A → Seed → Pre-seed → Series B
Pre-seed → Series A → Seed → Series B
Founders typically raise pre-seed money (often from themselves, friends or angels), then a seed round, followed by institutional Series A and later Series B rounds to scale.
A startup has ₹1.8 crore in the bank. Its monthly expenses are ₹45 lakh and monthly revenue is ₹15 lakh. Assuming these stay constant, what is its cash runway?
4 months
8 months
12 months
6 months
Net burn = ₹45 lakh − ₹15 lakh = ₹30 lakh per month. Runway = ₹180 lakh ÷ ₹30 lakh = 6 months. Using gross burn alone gives the wrong answer of 4 months.
An enterprise sells low-cost sanitary pads made by rural women's groups and reinvests most of its surplus to expand access in villages. This is best described as:
Social entrepreneurship
Corporate social responsibility
Franchising
Lifestyle entrepreneurship
Social entrepreneurship uses a business model whose primary aim is social impact, reinvesting surplus towards that mission. CSR is spending by an existing company, not the core business itself.
An employee of a large bank develops and launches a new digital lending product within the bank, using its resources. Such behaviour is called:
Outsourcing
Franchising
Intrapreneurship
Disintermediation
Intrapreneurship means acting like an entrepreneur inside an existing organisation, taking initiative and risk to create new products while using the employer's resources.
In a SWOT analysis of a startup, a large competitor announcing entry into the same market would be classified as a:
Weakness
Strength
Threat
Opportunity
Strengths and weaknesses are internal; opportunities and threats are external. A new competitor is an external factor that could harm the firm, so it is a threat.
The 'Blue Ocean Strategy' proposed by W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne recommends that firms:
create uncontested market space that makes competition irrelevant
cut prices aggressively to win share from existing competitors
focus only on the largest and most crowded existing markets
copy successful rivals quickly and improve on their products
Blue oceans are new, uncontested markets created through value innovation; red oceans are crowded markets where firms fight over existing demand, often through price cuts.
A restaurant chain keeps its spice-blend recipe confidential among a few staff bound by non-disclosure agreements instead of applying for a patent. The recipe is protected as a:
Trademark
Copyright
Geographical Indication
Trade secret
A trade secret is valuable confidential information protected by secrecy and contracts. Unlike a patent, it never requires public disclosure and can last indefinitely if kept secret.
A founder owns 60% of a company's 1,00,000 shares. The company then issues 25,000 new shares to an investor. What is the founder's stake after this issue?
The founder still holds 60,000 shares, but the total rises to 1,25,000. Stake = 60,000 ÷ 1,25,000 = 48%. This reduction in ownership is called dilution.
In the design thinking process (Empathise, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test), which stage comes immediately after defining the problem?
Ideate
Empathise
Prototype
Test
After empathising with users and defining the problem, teams ideate by generating many possible solutions, then build prototypes and test them. The process is iterative.

Language Comprehension.overview: Language Comprehension in MAT tests everyday command of English. Expect synonyms and antonyms, idioms, one-word substitution, fill-in-the-blank with vocabulary and prepositions, error spotting based on subject-verb agreement and tense, sentence rearrangement, direct and indirect speech, active and passive voice, spellings, and short reading passages with main-idea, detail, vocabulary-in-context and inference questions. Revise core grammar rules, build vocabulary through regular reading, and for passages answer only from what the text actually says rather than from outside knowledge.
questions: A meticulous editor checks every comma twice. Which word is a synonym of 'meticulous' here?
Painstaking
Careless
Indifferent
Hasty
Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, which is what painstaking means. Careless and hasty are nearly opposite, and indifferent means lacking interest.
Ravi is frugal: he cooks at home and saves most of his salary. Pick the antonym of 'frugal'.
Economical
Extravagant
Prudent
Thrifty
Frugal means careful and sparing with money. Extravagant, meaning spending lavishly, is its opposite. Thrifty and economical are synonyms, and prudent is close in sense.
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'a red herring'.
An embarrassing mistake made in public
A rare and valuable opportunity that should be seized
A warning sign of danger ahead
Something that distracts attention from the real issue

A red herring is a misleading clue or irrelevant point that draws attention away from the main question, common in debates and detective stories. It has nothing to do with danger signs or opportunities.
Choose the one word for: 'a person who can speak several languages'.
Polymath
Ventriloquist
Polyglot
Bibliophile
A polyglot knows or speaks many languages. A polymath has wide learning in many subjects, a bibliophile loves books, and a ventriloquist throws his voice.

Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
The committee's report was so ______ that even experts struggled to follow its argument.
concise
lucid
convoluted
candid
'Even experts struggled to follow' signals a report that was complicated and hard to follow, which is convoluted. Lucid and concise would make it easy to follow; candid concerns honesty, not clarity.

Fill in the blank with the correct preposition.
She has been working in this company ______ 2019.
for
from
by
since
With the present perfect continuous, 'since' is used before a point in time (2019) and 'for' before a period (five years). 'From' needs an end point such as 'to 2023'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither the manager nor his assistants / was present / at the meeting / held yesterday.
held yesterday
was present
at the meeting
Neither the manager nor his assistants
With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Assistants' is plural, so the verb should be 'were present', not 'was present'.

Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
He is one of those leaders / who has always / put the country / before himself.
who has always
He is one of those leaders
before himself
put the country
In 'one of those leaders who…', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural 'leaders', so the verb must be plural: 'who have always put the country before themselves'.

The first sentence is given. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph.
1. The monsoon is vital to Indian agriculture.
P. As a result, a delayed or weak monsoon can hurt farm output and rural incomes.
Q. A large part of the country's farmland depends on rainfall rather than irrigation.
R. This, in turn, can push up food prices in towns and cities.
S. Policymakers therefore track the monsoon's progress closely.
PQRS
QPRS
QPSR
QRPS
Q explains why the monsoon is vital; P gives the result ('As a result'); R extends the effect to cities ('in turn'); S concludes ('therefore'). Hence QPRS.
Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, "I will finish the report tomorrow."
He told that he would finish the report the next day.
He said that I would finish the report the next day.
He said that he would finish the report the next day.
He said that he will finish the report tomorrow.
In reported speech after a past reporting verb, 'will' becomes 'would', 'I' becomes 'he' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'. 'Told' needs an object, so 'He told that' is incorrect.
Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
Millenium
Occurence
Embarassment
Accommodate
Accommodate has double 'c' and double 'm'. The correct spellings of the others are occurrence (double r), embarrassment (double r and double s) and millennium (double l and double n).

Read the passage and answer the question.

Stepwells, found mainly in Gujarat and Rajasthan, were built to reach groundwater that sank far below the surface in the dry months. Flights of steps led down several storeys to the water, so that people could draw it whatever its level. Because the lower levels stayed cooler than the scorching ground above, stepwells also served as places of rest and social gathering, and many were richly carved. Under colonial rule, piped water and hand-pumps were promoted as more hygienic, and many stepwells fell into neglect, some becoming dumps for rubbish. Today a number are being restored, not only as heritage sites but also as a way of recharging groundwater in regions where it is being rapidly depleted.

According to the passage, stepwells had long flights of steps mainly:
to give access to water whose level changed through the year
to display the wealth of their builders
to keep animals away from the water
to provide seating for large public ceremonies held at the well
The passage says steps led down several storeys 'so that people could draw it whatever its level', because groundwater sank in the dry months. The other purposes are not stated.

Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a role of stepwells?
Providing access to groundwater
Serving as a place for social gathering
Offering a cool place to rest
Storing grain during famines
The passage mentions access to groundwater, cool lower levels for rest, and social gathering. Storage of grain is never mentioned, so it is the answer.

As used in the passage, the word 'depleted' most nearly means:
used up
measured
polluted
replenished

Depleted means reduced or exhausted. Restoring stepwells to recharge groundwater makes sense only if groundwater is being used up. 'Replenished' is the opposite, and 'polluted' changes quality, not quantity.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
Piped water reached the stepwell regions only after independence.
Stepwells may have practical value beyond their historical importance.
All the stepwells in Rajasthan have now been fully restored.
Stepwells were built mainly to store rainwater for temples.

Restoration is valued 'not only as heritage sites but also' for recharging groundwater, which shows a practical value. The passage says only 'a number' are being restored and links piped water to colonial rule.

Intelligence & Critical Reasoning.overview: Intelligence and Critical Reasoning in MAT combines verbal and non-verbal reasoning with critical thinking. Common topics are number and letter series, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions, syllogisms, seating and ranking, analogies, odd one out, clocks and calendars, and statement-based questions on assumptions, courses of action and strengthening or weakening arguments. Practise by drawing diagrams for relations and directions, using Venn diagrams for syllogisms, and checking every condition in arrangement puzzles. For critical reasoning, identify the conclusion first and look for the option that attacks or supports the link to it.
questions:
Find the next term of the series.
3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
The terms are n² − 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35. The next is 7² − 1 = 48. Equivalently, the differences 5, 7, 9, 11 continue with 13.

Find the next letter of the series.
A, C, F, J, O, ?
V
U
T
S
The gaps increase by one each time: +2, +3, +4, +5. The next gap is +6, and O (15) + 6 = U (21).
In a certain code, LAMP is written as OZNK. How will GOLD be written in that code?
TLOW
TMOW
TLOX
SLOW
Each letter is replaced by its mirror letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on; positions add up to 27). G→T, O→L, L→O, D→W, giving TLOW.
Pointing to a man, Meera said, "His father is the only son of my father's father." How is the man related to Meera?
Uncle
Cousin
Brother
Nephew
The only son of Meera's paternal grandfather is Meera's own father. So the man's father is Meera's father, which makes the man her brother.
Ravi walks 5 km south, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 9 km. How far and in which direction is he now from his starting point?
7 km, North-East
5 km, North-West
4 km, North
5 km, North-East
Facing south, a left turn means east (3 km); another left means north (9 km). Net position: 3 km east and 4 km north, so he is √(9 + 16) = 5 km away towards the north-east.

Statements:
No doctor is a lawyer.
Some lawyers are writers.
Conclusions:
I. Some writers are not doctors.
II. Some doctors are writers.
Both conclusions follow
Neither conclusion follows
Only conclusion II follows
Only conclusion I follows
The writers who are lawyers cannot be doctors, since no doctor is a lawyer, so some writers are certainly not doctors. Nothing links doctors to writers directly, so II is only a possibility.

Statement: The city council has decided to plant 10,000 saplings along highways to reduce air pollution.
Assumptions:
I. Trees can help reduce air pollution.
II. Air pollution in the city is caused only by vehicles on highways.
Which assumption is implicit?
Only assumption II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Only assumption I is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
The decision makes sense only if trees help reduce pollution, so I is implicit. The council need not believe highways are the only source; planting along them can help even if other sources exist.

A shop moved its umbrellas next to the entrance, and umbrella sales over the following month rose by 40%. The manager concluded that the new placement caused the rise. Which of the following, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
The month after the move had unusually heavy and frequent rain.
The shop also sells raincoats, which were kept in their original place.
Umbrellas at the shop are priced slightly below those of nearby stores.
Customers notice items placed near the entrance more often than others.

Heavy rain offers an alternative cause for higher umbrella sales, weakening the claim that placement was responsible. The point about customers noticing entrance items would actually support the manager's conclusion.
In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 14th from the left end. Kiran is 9th to the right of Ravi. What is Kiran's position from the right end?
17th
18th
19th
23rd
Kiran is 14 + 9 = 23rd from the left. Position from the right = 40 − 23 + 1 = 18th. 23rd is his position from the left, a common trap.

Select the word that completes the analogy.
Ornithology : Birds :: Entomology : ?
Fossils
Words
Insects
Fungi
Ornithology is the study of birds; entomology is the study of insects. Words are studied in etymology, fungi in mycology and fossils in palaeontology.
Select the letter group that does NOT belong with the others.
RTW
BDF
HJL
MOQ
In BDF, HJL and MOQ, each letter is two places after the previous one. In RTW the gaps are two and then three (R→T→W), so it is the odd one out.
What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:40?
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30 × 3 − 5.5 × 40| = |90 − 220| = 130°. Ignoring the hour hand's movement past 3 would wrongly give 120°.

Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north.
• B sits second to the left of D.
• E sits immediately to the right of B.
• A sits at one of the ends, to the left of C.
• C is not next to A.
Who sits in the middle?
C
B
D
E
A must be at the left end. B, E, D occupy three consecutive seats (B, E, then D), and C cannot be next to A, so the order is A, B, E, D, C. E is in the middle.

Statement: Several cases of food poisoning were reported after a wedding feast in a town.
Courses of action:
I. The health department should collect samples of the food served and investigate.
II. All weddings in the town should be banned for a year.
Which course of action follows?
Neither I nor II follows
Only I follows
Both I and II follow
Only II follows
Investigating the food is a practical step to find the cause and prevent repetition. Banning all weddings is an extreme reaction that does not address the actual problem, so only I follows.
If 15 August 2026 falls on a Saturday, on which day will 15 August 2027 fall?
Monday
Saturday
Sunday
Friday
The period from 15 August 2026 to 15 August 2027 contains February 2027, which is not a leap month, so there are 365 days, or 1 odd day. Saturday + 1 = Sunday.

Mathematical Skills.overview: Mathematical Skills in MAT covers school-level arithmetic, algebra, geometry and mensuration. Key topics include percentages, profit and loss with discounts, simple and compound interest, ratio and partnership, mixtures and alligation, averages, ages, time and work, time-speed-distance with trains and boats, number properties such as HCF and LCM, quadratic equations, permutations and combinations, and basic probability. Revise standard formulas and shortcuts, practise mental calculation, and watch for common traps such as changing bases in percentage questions and overlaps in probability.
questions: What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹12,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum (compounded annually)?
For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 12,000 × 0.01 = ₹120. CI = ₹2,520 and SI = ₹2,400, confirming the difference.
A's income is 20% less than B's. By what percentage is B's income more than A's?
If B = 100, A = 80. B exceeds A by 20 on a base of 80, i.e. 20/80 × 100 = 25%. The base changes, so the answer is not 20%.
A starts a business with ₹30,000. After 4 months, B joins with ₹40,000. Out of a profit of ₹17,000 at the end of the year, what is B's share?
In what ratio must rice costing ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹55 per kg to get a mixture worth ₹45 per kg?
Two trains 150 m and 100 m long run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long will they take to cross each other completely?
25 seconds
9 seconds
10 seconds
12.5 seconds
Relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance = 150 + 100 = 250 m. Time = 250/25 = 10 seconds. Using the difference of speeds would wrongly give 25 seconds.
The average of 11 numbers is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and that of the last six is 52. What is the sixth number?
The sixth number is counted in both groups: 6 × 49 + 6 × 52 − 11 × 50 = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56.
Five years ago, the ratio of the ages of A and B was 3 : 4. Five years from now, it will be 5 : 6. What is A's present age?
30 years
25 years
15 years
20 years
Let ages five years ago be 3k and 4k. Then (3k + 10)/(4k + 10) = 5/6, so 18k + 60 = 20k + 50 and k = 5. A is 15 + 5 = 20 years now.
An article marked at ₹1,200 is sold at a 15% discount and the seller still makes a 20% profit. What is its cost price?
Selling price = 85% of 1,200 = ₹1,020. Since this includes 20% profit, cost price = 1,020/1.2 = ₹850. Taking 20% off 1,020 wrongly gives ₹816.
What is the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by 6, 8 or 12, and is exactly divisible by 11?
Such numbers have the form 24k + 4 (LCM of 6, 8, 12 is 24). Testing k = 1, 2, 3, …, the first divisible by 11 is k = 9: 24 × 9 + 4 = 220 = 11 × 20.
Three ropes of 84 m, 126 m and 210 m are to be cut into pieces of equal length, as long as possible, with nothing left over. How many pieces will there be in all?
The greatest common length is HCF(84, 126, 210) = 42 m. Pieces = 84/42 + 126/42 + 210/42 = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.
A right circular cone has base radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm. What is its volume? (Take π = 22/7)
Height = √(25² − 7²) = 24 cm. Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 49 × 24 = 1,232 cm³. Forgetting the 1/3 gives 3,696 cm³.
If α and β are the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0, what is the value of α² + β²?
α + β = 7 and αβ = 12. So α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 49 − 24 = 25. The roots 3 and 4 confirm: 9 + 16 = 25.
In how many different ways can the letters of the word MANAGER be arranged?
MANAGER has 7 letters with A repeated twice and the rest distinct. Arrangements = 7!/2! = 5,040/2 = 2,520.
A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king or a heart?
Kings: 4, hearts: 13, king of hearts counted twice: 1. Favourable = 4 + 13 − 1 = 16, so probability = 16/52 = 4/13. Not subtracting the overlap gives 17/52.
Walking at three-fourths of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 20 minutes late. What is his usual time for the journey?
45 minutes
80 minutes
60 minutes
40 minutes
At 3/4 of the speed, time becomes 4/3 of usual. Extra time = (4/3 − 1) × t = t/3 = 20 minutes, so t = 60 minutes.

Data Analysis & Sufficiency.overview: Data Analysis and Sufficiency in MAT presents data in tables, pie charts, bar and line graphs, and asks for totals, averages, percentages, ratios and growth rates. It also includes data sufficiency questions, where you decide whether the given statements are enough to answer a question rather than computing the answer itself. Practise quick percentage and ratio calculations, read the units and base of every chart carefully, and for sufficiency questions test each statement alone before combining them, without assuming facts not stated.
questions:
Students enrolled in four courses at an institute:
Course | 2022 | 2023 | 2024
BBA | 400 | 460 | 520
BCom | 600 | 570 | 630
BSc | 350 | 420 | 490
BA | 250 | 260 | 240

By what percentage did the total enrolment rise from 2022 to 2024?

Students enrolled in four courses at an institute:
Course | 2022 | 2023 | 2024
BBA | 400 | 460 | 520
BCom | 600 | 570 | 630
BSc | 350 | 420 | 490
BA | 250 | 260 | 240

BSc enrolment in 2024 was what percentage of BBA enrolment in 2022?
BSc 2024 = 490 and BBA 2022 = 400. 490/400 × 100 = 122.5%. Take care to compare the right course and the right year.

Students enrolled in four courses at an institute:
Course | 2022 | 2023 | 2024
BBA | 400 | 460 | 520
BCom | 600 | 570 | 630
BSc | 350 | 420 | 490
BA | 250 | 260 | 240

In how many courses was the 2024 enrolment more than 20% higher than the 2022 enrolment?
BBA rose 30% (400 to 520) and BSc 40% (350 to 490). BCom rose only 5% and BA fell 4%. So two courses qualify.

A company's annual budget of ₹45 crore is allocated as: Production 40%, Salaries 20%, Marketing 18%, R&D 12%, Administration 10%.

What central angle would represent R&D in a pie chart of this budget?
Central angle = share × 360°. R&D = 12% of 360° = 43.2°. 36° corresponds to Administration's 10%.

A company's annual budget of ₹45 crore is allocated as: Production 40%, Salaries 20%, Marketing 18%, R&D 12%, Administration 10%.

By how much does the Marketing allocation exceed the Administration allocation?
₹3.2 crore
₹8 crore
₹4.5 crore
₹3.6 crore
Marketing − Administration = 18% − 10% = 8% of ₹45 crore = ₹3.6 crore. ₹8 crore mistakes the percentage gap for a rupee amount.

Annual profit (₹ lakh) of a firm: 2020 – 35, 2021 – 42, 2022 – 38, 2023 – 50, 2024 – 60.

In which year was the percentage increase in profit over the previous year the highest?
Changes: 2021 +20%, 2022 −9.5%, 2023 +31.6% (38 to 50), 2024 +20%. 2024 has the largest absolute rise (10), but 2023 has the highest percentage rise.

Annual profit (₹ lakh) of a firm: 2020 – 35, 2021 – 42, 2022 – 38, 2023 – 50, 2024 – 60.

By what percentage was the 2024 profit higher than the average annual profit for 2020–2024?

In a survey of 500 people, 300 were men and 200 were women. 180 of the men and 90 of the women preferred tea; everyone else preferred coffee.

What percentage of the people who preferred coffee were women?
Coffee: men 300 − 180 = 120, women 200 − 90 = 110, total 230. Women's share = 110/230 × 100 ≈ 47.8%. 55% is the share of women who prefer coffee, a different base.

In a survey of 500 people, 300 were men and 200 were women. 180 of the men and 90 of the women preferred tea; everyone else preferred coffee.

What is the ratio of people who preferred tea to those who preferred coffee?
Tea = 180 + 90 = 270; coffee = 500 − 270 = 230. Ratio 270 : 230 = 27 : 23. Reversing the order gives 23 : 27.

The question is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer it.

What is the value of the integer x?
I. x² = 16
II. x > 0
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed, but neither alone is sufficient
Each statement alone is sufficient
I alone gives x = 4 or −4, and II alone gives any positive integer. Together they fix x = 4, so both are needed.

The question is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer it.

What is the cost price of an article?
I. It was sold for ₹550 at a profit of 10%.
II. It was marked at ₹700 and sold at a discount of ₹150.
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
Each statement alone is sufficient
Both statements together are needed, but neither alone is sufficient
I gives cost price = 550/1.1 = ₹500. II gives only the selling price (₹550) with no profit information, so it cannot give the cost price.

The question is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer it.

Is the integer n divisible by 6?
I. n is divisible by 12.
II. n is divisible by both 2 and 3.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed, but neither alone is sufficient
Each statement alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Any multiple of 12 is a multiple of 6, so I answers 'yes'. Divisibility by both 2 and 3 (coprime) also means divisibility by 6. Each statement alone suffices.

The question is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer it.

How many days will B alone take to finish a piece of work?
I. A and B together finish it in 6 days.
II. A alone finishes it in 10 days.
Both statements together are needed, but neither alone is sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
Each statement alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Neither statement alone gives B's rate. Together, B's rate = 1/6 − 1/10 = 1/15, so B takes 15 days. Both are needed.

The question is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer it.

What is the speed of a boat in still water?
I. The speed of the stream is 2 km/h.
II. The boat goes 24 km downstream in 2 hours and returns upstream in 3 hours.
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed, but neither alone is sufficient
Each statement alone is sufficient
II gives downstream speed 12 km/h and upstream 8 km/h, so still-water speed = (12 + 8)/2 = 10 km/h. I alone gives only the stream's speed.

The question is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer it.

Who is the tallest among P, Q and R?
I. P is taller than Q but shorter than R.
II. R is taller than Q.
Both statements together are needed, but neither alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Each statement alone is sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
I gives the full order R > P > Q, so R is tallest. II says nothing about P, who could be taller or shorter than R.

Introduction to Insurance.overview: This chapter introduces risk and how insurance handles it. Learners should be clear on the difference between risk, peril and hazard; physical and moral hazard; pure and speculative risk; and the main risk-management techniques of avoidance, retention, reduction and transfer. It also explains how pooling and the law of large numbers allow insurers to predict losses, the primary and secondary burdens of risk, the basic rules for deciding what to insure, and how reinsurance lets insurers spread very large risks. Focus on applying these terms to everyday scenarios rather than memorising definitions.
questions: In a fire policy covering a warehouse, the fire itself is best described as the:
Hazard
Moral hazard
Peril
Risk premium
